atevaññehi.meaning_2: with more than the other eleven; with eleven months more than the others
atevaññehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Likely sandhi of ati + eva + aññehi (añña instrumental plural); alternative atīva + aññehi. Instrumental plural agreeing with māsehi.
atevaññehi.translation_1: it shines with the flowers of trees much more than other eleven months.

atevaññehīti.meaning_2: by those not despising; with those who do not scorn
atevaññehīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Contains the emphatic/closing particle iti (-ti) in the text. Resolves as ati (veda) aññehi, i.e. ati + eva + aññehi, "by the not-despising ones". Instrumental plural.

vāhiyeti.meaning_2: causes to be carried; has (it) conveyed; makes carry
vāhiyeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative-passive-looking form; related to vāhiya 'to be carried'. In the text it may stand for the causative vāheti. No sentence supplied, so the meaning is inferred.

bahīpureti.meaning_2: outside and inside; here and there
bahīpureti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of bahi (outside) + pure (before, in front, earlier) + iti (quotation mark). No sentences were supplied, so the analysis is uncertain; bahī is the sandhi form of bahi before a vowel, and pure can also be a locative of pura (city), giving the alternative bahi pure iti.

selento.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine singular selento from selayati; in the text it describes the crowd, meaning 'shouting'. The root is uncertain.
selento.example_1: Mahājano nadanto selento apphoṭento sādhukārasahassāni adāsi, celukkhepe ca aṅguliphoṭe ca pavattesi, hatthapiḷandhanādīni khipi.
selento.translation_1: The great mass of people, roaring, shouting, and clapping their hands, gave thousands of shouts of approval. They also caused the waving of cloths and snapping of fingers to arise, and they cast off their bracelets and other hand ornaments.

byamhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In text as byamhito, nominative singular masculine. Grammarians derive it from vi + mih (smile) with bya- for vi-, or from Vimhaya + ita; the commentarial gloss is bhīto vimhayamāpanno. Doublet of vimhita.
byamhito.example_1: Avaca byamhito rājā, yakkhānaṃ katamo nusi.
byamhito.translation_1: the king, being terrified, spoke: ‘Which of the ogres are you?’
byamhito.translation_2: Terrified (byamhito) means afraid or struck with amazement.

duddasī.meaning_2: ugly; of unpleasant appearance; difficult to look at
duddasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it is a nominative singular adjective describing the speaker; the gloss explains it as dukkhena passitabbo. The PEU analysis du + disa + ṇī treats -ī as a possessive suffix, so store the stem as duddas-.
duddasī.translation_1: 184. ‘Ugly and misshapen you are, of ill-color and scary to see;
duddasī.translation_2: Ugly (duddasī) means one who is to be seen with difficulty (or unpleasant to see).

byamhitoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form appears with the quotative -ti (byamhito + ti). The prefix vi- is written bya- by sandhi of v + y. The alternative analysis is byamhita as a past participle of a denominative byamhati from byamha, 'fear, terror'; the quoted source links it to Vimhaya and ibha. Nom. sg. masc. in the text.

pasupī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular; the form pasupī has a variant ending -ī. The whole line is metrical: evaṃ me parittātūna, pasupī so muhuttakaṃ. The meaning given is 'slept' (cf. √sup 'lie down, sleep'); form uncertain, possibly an irregular aorist or a sandhi of pasupi with a following pronoun.
pasupī.example_1: 204. ‘‘ Evaṃ me parittātūna, pasupī so muhuttakaṃ;
pasupī.translation_1: 204. “Thus, having entrusted his protection to me, he slept for a moment.

paṭilacchiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of paṭilabhati (√labh + a > labha, with aorist ending -iṃ; double c is by sandhi before the ending). In the text it governs diṭṭhiṃ: 'I conceived (such) a view'.
paṭilacchiṃ.translation_1: Then I unwisely conceived a distorted perspective:

sannitāḷayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist. The simplex √taḷ means 'to beat'; the prefixed causative form means 'to strike down'. The PEU analysis with ṇaya is unexpected; the usual causative suffix is *aya.
sannitāḷayiṃ.translation_1: 207. “Then, taking a stone, I struck him on the head.

pakkhalya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -ya (pakkhalya = pakkhalitvā). In the text it takes the object matthakaṃ: 'having washed his head'. The PEU analysis (pa + khala + tvā) gives the same sense.
pakkhalya.example_1: 215. ‘‘ Idaṃ vatvā giricaro, rahade pakkhalya matthakaṃ;
pakkhalya.translation_1: 215. ‘‘Having said this, the mountain-dweller washed his head in the pool,

sampamajjitvā.meaning_2: having wiped off; having wiped away; having cleaned
sampamajjitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive describing the wiping away of tears (assūni) before climbing the mountain.
sampamajjitvā.translation_1: and having wiped away his tears, he then ascended the mountain.

tāvanto.meaning_2: that many; so many; of that extent; such an amount (of)
tāvanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Correlative with yāvant. Nominative singular masculine in the text, agreeing with ubbegā. Often written tāvanto as nominative plural masculine in related forms.
tāvanto.translation_1: —that many tumors arose, the size of half a bilva fruit.
tāvanto.example_2: Tāvanto tassa ubbegā, tasmā guyhaṃ na vissaje;
tāvanto.translation_2: so many anxieties arise for him. Therefore, one should not reveal a secret.

māgañchīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Quoted form mā añchi (mā + agacchi) in the text, written māgañchīti with a corrupt or phonetic sandhi; the -ti is the quotative particle. Aorist 3rd singular in a prohibitive sense.

sannitāḷayinti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The reading sannitāḷayinti is likely sannitāḷayiṃ with the quotative -ti (sandhi), an aorist/causative 1st person singular: 'I beat'. PEU splits it as saṃ + ni + tāḷa + ṇaya + iṃ.

sannitāḷayantipi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form is sannitāḷayantipi, with -pi. Causal of nitāḷayati (to fan).

udappattoti.meaning_2: flying up; risen and gone away; one who has got up and run off
udappattoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is the quotation particle; the text form is udappatto ti. The split is uncertain; possibly ud + patta (√pat, fallen) or ud + appatta, or a compound with pada. Not a common DPD headword.

māyyoti.meaning_2: one connected with māyā; deceiver; sorcerer
māyyoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Uncertain. The form māyyoti looks like māyyo + ti from a text. Could also be māyā + ya, or a variant reading. Meaning guessed; not found in the given sentences.

mantiādimāha.meaning_2: said 'mantī etc.'; spoke the words beginning 'manti'
mantiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound quotation + āha. Probably manti + ādi + māha variant; āha = √ah + a (perf 3sg). Sandhi of a compound word and a verb.

pakkhalyāti.meaning_2: having washed off; having rinsed; having cleansed
pakkhalyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form pakkhalyāti is pakkhalya + iti; the absolutive here has the -ya ending (for -tvā). The PEU entry connects it to 'clean'. The reading is uncertain; compare pakkhāleti (washes).

okkitāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form okkitāti is okkitā + iti; the -ā is the nominative singular masculine ending, so the headword is the participle okkita. Often explained as ava + kira + ta, 'strewn (with), surrounded (by)'. The final -ti belongs to the quotation particle iti.

votiādimāha.meaning_2: voti ādi + māha: said 'voti' at the beginning; uttered 'voti' first
votiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of voti, ādi and māha (√ah, perfect). The word is evidently a quotation followed by ādi-m-āha 'said ... first'. No sentence was supplied, so the analysis is provisional.

mudīreti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present in the verse; causative form meaning 'causes to be spoken' i.e. utters.
mudīreti.example_1: 264. ‘‘ Tirokkhavāco asataṃ paviṭṭho, yo saṅgatīsu mudīreti vākyaṃ;
mudīreti.translation_1: 264. “One who is deceptive in speech, who has entered the company of the wicked, and utters such words in assemblies—

tyamhāti.meaning_2: therefore?; from that?; it is from that
tyamhāti.construction: tyaṃ + ha + iti? / tya + amhā + iti?
tyamhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] No sentences were supplied, so the analysis is uncertain. Probably a sandhi of iti with a preceding word ending in -tyaṃ, -tvā or an ablative; if the whole is a quotation the final -ti is an enclitic and the entry may rather belong to the main word. Treat as provisional.

paṇḍarakanāgaṃ.meaning_2: Paṇḍaraka the nāga king; the serpent-king Paṇḍaraka
paṇḍarakanāgaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a nāga king in the Jātaka commentary. Accusative singular in both sentences.
paṇḍarakanāgaṃ.example_1: Bhayaṃ tamanvetīti taṃ imehi catūhi aṅgehi samannāgataṃ abodhaṃ duppaññaṃ puggalaṃ sayaṃkatameva bhayaṃ anveti, yathā maṃ paṇḍarakanāgaṃ supaṇṇo anvāgatoti.
paṇḍarakanāgaṃ.translation_1: Fear follows him (bhayaṃ tamanvetī) means that a self-created peril follows such an ignorant and unwise person who is endowed with these four factors, just as the Garuda followed me, Paṇḍaraka the snake-king.
paṇḍarakanāgaṃ.translation_2: O double-tongued one (dujivhā) addresses the Nāga King Paṇḍaraka.

mudīretīti.meaning_2: causes to be happy; gladdens; cheers; (it is) said to make joyful
mudīretīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in the text is mudīreti, with -ī- perhaps metrical or by analogy with hīreti type forms; the final -ti of the text is the quotative particle -iti here, so the entry is for the verb alone. Causative of mudīrati; cf. pamudita. Grammar uncertain.

asmiṃdha.meaning_2: in this here; here in this
asmiṃdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of asmiṃ (locative singular of ima) + idha. Locative in the verse; asmiṃdha can also be analysed as asmiṃ + iha. See also loke in the same line.
asmiṃdha.example_1: 266. ‘‘ Ko nīdha tiṇṇaṃ garahaṃ upeti, asmiṃdha loke pāṇabhū nāgarāja;
asmiṃdha.translation_1: 266. “Who among these three people here in this world, O snake-king, now incurs blame?

paṇḍarakaggahītoti.meaning_2: seized by a white horse; grasped by a pale horse
paṇḍarakaggahītoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of paṇḍarakaggahīto (or paṇḍarakehi gahīto) with the quotation particle ti; the reading and segmentation are uncertain.

asmiṃdhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Not found in the text. Likely a sandhi of asmiṃ (locative of ayaṃ, 'in this') + dhāti, perhaps a quotation embedded in the commentary.

paṇḍaraka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a mythical bird. In the text it is the vocative singular, addressed as samma paṇḍaraka. The compound paṇḍarakaggahīto contains the same word; the commentary glosses it with the vocative.
paṇḍaraka.example_1: Paṇḍarakaggahītoti, samma paṇḍaraka,‘‘ ahaṃ kiṃkāraṇā supaṇṇena gahito ’’ ti cintetvā ca pana attānameva garaha, tayā hi rahassaṃ kathentena attanāva attano anattho katoti ayamettha adhippāyo.
paṇḍaraka.translation_1: Seized, Paṇḍara (paṇḍarakaggahīto) means: “Friend Paṇḍara, after thinking, ‘For what reason was I seized by the Garuda?’ you should instead blame yourself. For by telling the secret, you have brought about your own harm.” This is the intended meaning here.

alabbhamabyāharatī.meaning_2: a person obtains what is hard to obtain
alabbhamabyāharatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of alabbhaṃ (adjective, pp of labhati with na) and abyāharati (present 3rd singular of abyāharati, to obtain, bring); written abyāharatī with lengthened final vowel before naro. The line is a verse; some editions read alabbham abyāharatī.
alabbhamabyāharatī.example_1: Saccena dhammena dhitiyā damena, alabbhamabyāharatī naro idha.
alabbhamabyāharatī.translation_1: Here, a person achieves that which is hard to gain by truth, by Dhamma, by fortitude, and by self-control.

saṃhīro.meaning_2: deceitful; shifty; compliant; easily led astray
saṃhīro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text saṃhīro is nominative singular; in the commentary it is glossed as one who is enticed or persuaded by gain.
saṃhīro.example_1: Yo cāmisena saṃhīro, hadayattheno ca yo naro.
saṃhīro.translation_1: and whoever is shifty by temptation, and whoever is a thief of hearts.”
saṃhīro.example_2: Saṃhīroti yo ca yena kenaci āmisena saṃhīrati upalāpati saṅgahaṃ gacchati, tassapi na saṃseyya.
saṃhīro.translation_2: ‘One who is compliant’ means one who is enticed or persuaded by any kind of gain whatsoever, or who goes along with things; one should not confide in him either.

sambodhayati.meaning_2: makes known; reveals; discloses; brings to understanding
sambodhayati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of sambujjhati (saṃ + √budh). Here takes guyhamatthaṃ as object: 'reveals a secret matter'. 3rd singular present in the verse; the meter requires the long -a-. PEU records the saṃboheti variant.
sambodhayati.translation_1: “Whoever reveals a secret matter to an unwise person,

byavajanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the 3rd plural byavajanti; the entry is the 3rd singular. Doubtful: the prefix bya- is a written form of vi + ava, as the PEU's Vi+ava+aja+anti suggests; compare vyavajanti. Also doubtful: whether the root is √aj (go) or √vaj; the reading byavajanti is itself uncertain.
byavajanti.example_1: Ārā amittā byavajanti tehi, āsīvisā vā riva sattusaṅghā ’’ ti.
byavajanti.translation_1: from them, enemies flee far, just as people desiring to live flee far from groups of enemies who are like venomous snakes.”

byavajantīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] -ti is the quotation marker; the main word is byavajanti (3rd plural). by- is a sandhi form of vi- before a vowel.

rivāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of iva. In the text, rivāti = riva + iti; the commentary explains it as a comparison with sattusaṅghā.
rivāti.example_1: Āsīvisā vā riva sattusaṅghāti ettha vāti nipātamattaṃ, āsīvisā sattusaṅghā rivāti attho.
rivāti.translation_1: Regarding `or just as groups of enemies are like venomous snakes` (āsīvisā vā riva sattusaṅghā): here, `vā` is merely a particle; the meaning is ‘just as groups of enemies are like venomous snakes’.

apaggatāmhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably apagga + tāmhā + ti, i.e. apaggatā amhā ti, with sandhi of the final -ā before the quotative ti; ablative/separative sense with apa-. Alternative analysis: apagata + tā. Exact reading uncertain.

evaṃkaroyeva.meaning_2: by doing exactly this; just by acting in this way
evaṃkaroyeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of evaṃ + karo + eva; in the text it qualifies karonto and describes the manner of wholesome action. Could also be analysed as evaṃ + karoyeva.
evaṃkaroyeva.example_1: Tattha hiriyāti, samma nāgarāja, ajjhattabahiddhāsamuṭṭhānehi hirottappehi titikkhāsaṅkhātāya adhivāsanakhantiyā indriyadamena ca upeto akujjhanasīlo pisuṇavācaṃ pahāya taṇhāmamāyitāni ca hitvā pabbajjāya caranto samaṇo nāma hoti, evaṃkaroyeva ca etāni hirīādīni kusalāni karonto saggamupeti ṭhānanti.
evaṃkaroyeva.translation_1: In this context, with moral shame (hiriyā) means: “My friend, snake-king, one who is endowed with moral shame and moral dread arising from internal and external sources; with the patience that consists of endurance; and with self-control of the senses—such a one, being free from anger, having abandoned malicious speech, and having abandoned the attachments of craving while conducting himself in the monastic life, is called a recluse. By acting in just this way, performing these wholesome deeds such as moral shame, he achieves a heavenly state.”

dijinda.meaning_2: lord of the birds; king of birds
dijinda.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the bird-king (dijarāja) in the Jātaka verses. Vocative singular in the text.
dijinda.example_1: Evampi me tvaṃ pāturahu dijinda, mātāva puttaṃ anukampamāno ’’ ti.
dijinda.translation_1: So have you appeared to me, O king of birds, out of compassion, like a mother to her child.”
dijinda.example_2: Tassattho – yathā mātā tanujaṃ attano sarīrajātaṃ taruṇaṃ puttaṃ samphassataṃ disvā taṃ ure nipajjāpetvā thaññaṃ pāyentī puttasamphassena sabbaṃ attano gattaṃ phareti, napi mātā puttato bhāyati napi putto mātito, evampi me tvaṃ pāturahu pātubhūto dijinda dijarāja, tasmā mātāva puttaṃ mudukena hadayena anukampamāno maṃ passa, jīvitaṃ me dehīti.
dijinda.translation_2: Its meaning is: just as a mother, on seeing her own-born (tanuja) young son—born of her own body—and feeling him, lays him on her breast and nurses him, letting the touch of her son pervade her entire body; and just as the mother does not fear the son, nor the son the mother; so too have you appeared (pāturahu) to me, O king of birds (dijinda). Therefore, look upon me with compassion as a mother does her son, with a tender heart, and grant me my life.

bhumyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (with sandhi: bhūmi + yaṃ). Basis of the sandhi form bhumyaṃ.
bhumyaṃ.example_1: 284. ‘‘ Icceva vākyaṃ visajjī supaṇṇo, bhumyaṃ patiṭṭhāya dijo dujivhaṃ;
bhumyaṃ.translation_1: 284. “Having spoken thus, the bird landed on the ground and released the double-tongued one.

bhumyanti.meaning_2: on the ground, it is said; on the ground, thus
bhumyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably bhūmiyā + iti, or a similar sandhi of a locative of bhūmi with iti, at a verse line end. No sentences given, so the analysis is uncertain.

abhigutto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here it is a past participle agreeing with the addressee, paired with rakkhito as a synonym; the commentator's gloss gives abhigutta = rakkhita. It can also be read as a potential participle: 'worth protecting, to be guarded'.
abhigutto.example_1: Bhumyanti so sayampi bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhāya dijo taṃ dujivhaṃ samassāsento mutto ajja tvaṃ ito paṭṭhāya sabbabhayāni ativatto thale ca udake ca mayā abhigutto rakkhito hohīti āha.
abhigutto.translation_1: On the ground (bhumyaṃ) means that the bird himself landed on the ground and, consoling the double-tongued one, said: “From now on, you are free and have overcome all fears; you shall be guarded and protected by me on both land and water.”

paṇḍarakanāgo.meaning_2: Paṇḍaraka the nāga; the nāga king named Paṇḍaraka
paṇḍarakanāgo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a nāga in the Jātaka prose; nominative singular in the text.
paṇḍarakanāgo.example_1: Itaropi supaṇṇabhavanaṃ gantvā ‘‘ mayā paṇḍarakanāgo sapathaṃ katvā saddahāpetvā vissajjito, kīdisaṃ nu kho mayi tassa hadayaṃ, vīmaṃsissāmi nan ’’ ti nāgabhavanaṃ gantvā supaṇṇavātaṃ akāsi.
paṇḍarakanāgo.translation_1: The other one, returning to the abode of the Garudas, thought: “The snake Paṇḍaraka has been released by me after making an oath and gaining my trust. I wonder what his heart is like toward me? I will test him.” So he went to the abode of the nāgas and stirred up a Garuda-wind.

ḍaṃsitukāmo.meaning_2: wanting to bite; desiring to bite
ḍaṃsitukāmo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Tatpurisa compound with an infinitive as first member. Nominative singular agreeing with nāgo in the text.
ḍaṃsitukāmo.example_1: Taṃ disvā nāgo ‘‘ supaṇṇarājā maṃ gahetuṃ āgato bhavissatī ’’ ti maññamāno byāmasahassamattaṃ attabhāvaṃ māpetvā pāsāṇe ca vālukañca gilitvā bhāriyo hutvā naṅguṭṭhaṃ heṭṭhākatvā bhogamatthake phaṇaṃ dhārayamāno nipajjitvā supaṇṇarājānaṃ ḍaṃsitukāmo viya ahosi.
ḍaṃsitukāmo.translation_1: On seeing him, the snake thought: “The Garuda-king must have come to seize me.” Thinking this, he manifested a form a thousand fathoms long, and making himself heavy by swallowing stones and sand, he lay down with his tail tucked beneath him and his hood raised above his coils, as if wishing to bite the Garuda-king.

tyamhīti.meaning_2: this is in me?; 'it is in me', so it is said
tyamhīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Likely tyaṃ (nt, 'this') + ahi (ind/verb, 'is') + iti, quoted speech; doubtful, possibly tyam + hi + iti. No sentence context given.

sambulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name used in the Sambulā Jātaka; nominative singular in the text. The PEU analysis (sambhu + lā + a) is uncertain.
sambulā.example_1: Taṃ rājā vayappattaṃ uparajje patiṭṭhapesi, sambulā nāmassa aggamahesī ahosi uttamarūpadharā sarīrappabhāsampannā, nivāte jalamānā dīpasikhā viya khāyati.
sambulā.translation_1: The king appointed that son, when he reached maturity, as viceroy. His chief queen was named Sambulā; she possessed supreme beauty and was endowed with bodily radiance, appearing like a lamp-flame shining in a sheltered spot.
sambulā.example_2: Sambulā bahūhi upāyehi nivattiyamānāpi anivattitvāva ‘‘ ahaṃ taṃ sāmikaṃ araññe paṭijaggissāmī ’’ ti vatvā saddhiññeva nikkhami.
sambulā.translation_2: Sambulā, though urged by many means to turn back, did not turn back, but instead said, “I will take care of that husband in the wilderness,” and departed with him.

sampiṇḍitūru.meaning_2: with well-rounded thighs; with solid thighs
sampiṇḍitūru.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A bahubbīhi compound describing bodily beauty. It is the glossed word in the phrase sampiṇḍitūru uttamaūrulakkhaṇe, where the text explains saṃhitūrū by the compound sampiṇḍitūru.
sampiṇḍitūru.translation_1: Saṃhitūrū means with well-rounded thighs, possessing the characteristic of excellent thighs.

sambulāhaṃ.meaning_2: I, Sambulā; (homage to you) from Sambulā
sambulāhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sambulā (a proper name, the goddess who praises the Buddha) + ahaṃ. Sandhi with contraction of the final ā before the vowel; the sentence is taṃ bhante, sambulāhaṃ namatthu te.
sambulāhaṃ.example_1: Abhivādemi taṃ bhante, sambulāhaṃ namatthu te.
sambulāhaṃ.translation_1: I, Sambulā, salute you, venerable sir; homage to you.

uñchetvā.meaning_2: having gleaned; having gathered leftover grain
uñchetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -etvā of uñchati (√uñch + *e), used in the gloss vanaṃ uñchetvā uñchācariyaṃ caritvā; the reading vanamuñchāya in the text is probably a misreading of vanaṃ uñchāya.
uñchetvā.translation_1: Vanamuñchāya means having gleaned the forest and having wandered for gleaning.

sambule.meaning_2: Sambulā; name of a woman, the wife of the ascetic in the Sambulā Jātaka
sambule.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name, vocative singular in the text (sambule). The related entry gives a masc sambula as a thera and the story's name; the vocative here addresses the queen.
sambule.example_1: Sambule pariciṇṇena, ahaṃ bhattā bhavāmi te.
sambule.translation_1: Sambulā, what is the use of serving him? I will be your husband.”
sambule.example_2: 306. ‘‘ No ce tuvaṃ maheseyyaṃ, sambule kārayissasi;
sambule.translation_2: “Sambulā, if you will not let yourself be made my chief queen,

sambulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a queen in the Sambulā Jātaka. In the text it appears as sambulaṃ, the accusative singular.
sambulaṃ.example_1: Vane nāthaṃ apassantiṃ, sambulaṃ aggahī bhuje.
sambulaṃ.translation_1: seized Sambulā by the arm as she looked about the forest, finding no protector.
sambulaṃ.example_2: Maheseyyanti,‘‘ bhadde, sambule no ce me tvaṃ mahesibhāvaṃ kāressasi, pariyattā tvaṃ mama pātarāsāya, tena taṃ balakkārena vimānaṃ nessāmi, tatra maṃ asaṅgaṇhantī mama sve pātova bhakkhā bhavissasī ’’ ti evaṃ vatvā so sattahi jaṭāhi samannāgato luddako dāruṇo nikkhantadanto taṃ tasmiṃ vane kiñci attano nāthaṃ apassantiṃ sambulaṃ bhuje aggahesi.
sambulaṃ.translation_2: Maheseyyan (maheseyyaṃ) means: “Good lady, Sambulā, if you will not allow me to make you my chief queen (mahesibhāvaṃ), you are already prepared (pariyattā) for my breakfast (pātarāsāya); therefore, I will take you to my mansion by force (balakkārena); there, if you do not attend to me (asaṅgaṇhantī), you will become my food (bhakkhā) early tomorrow morning (sve pātova).” Having said this, that savage (luddako), grim (dāruṇo) goblin with protruding fangs (nikkhantadanto), possessing seven matted locks (sattahi jaṭāhi), seized (aggahesi) Sambulā by the arm in that forest as she found no protector (nāthaṃ) for herself.

paḷinaṃ.meaning_2: abandoned; left; forsaken; empty (of a nest)
paḷinaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text glossed by paḷinattā (having flown away / been abandoned) and applied to a bird's nest (sakuṇinīḷaṃ). Variant reading palina. Could also be analysed as pp of paḷiyati/paḷīyati, but the commentary treats it as an adjective qualifying nīḷaṃ; accusative singular here.
paḷinaṃ.translation_1: just as a bird returns to its nest after being away, or a cow returns to its shed having lost its calf.
paḷinaṃ.example_2: Tattha nīḷaṃ paḷinaṃ sakuṇīvāti yathā sakuṇikā mukhatuṇḍakena gocaraṃ gahetvā kenaci upaddavena sakuṇapotakānaṃ paḷinattā paḷinaṃ sakuṇinīḷaṃ āgaccheyya, yathā vā gatasiṅgaṃ nikkhantavacchakaṃ ālayaṃ suññaṃ vacchakasālaṃ vacchagiddhinī dhenu āgaccheyya, evaṃ suññaṃ assamaṃ āgacchīti attho.
paḷinaṃ.translation_2: Therein, nīḷaṃ paḷinaṃ sakuṇīvā means just as a female bird, having taken food with its beak, might return to its abandoned bird's nest because its young birds have flown away due to some trouble. Or, gatasiṅgaṃ, meaning having lost its calf, just as a cow longing for its calf might return to an empty calf shed. The meaning is that she thus returned to the empty hermitage.

latāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text this is part of the compound tiṇā latāni, which is a sandhi of tiṇā and latāni; latāni is the accusative plural of latā. The word refers to creepers or climbing plants in the verse. See also tiṇa.
latāni.example_1: 316. ‘‘ Tiṇā latāni osajho, pabbatāni vanāni ca;
latāni.translation_1: 316. ‘‘ Hail to grasses, creepers, and herbs, to mountains and forests—
latāni.example_2: Tiṇā latāni osajhoti antopheggubahisāratiṇāni ca latāni ca antosāraosadhiyo ca.
latāni.translation_2: Tiṇā latāni osajho means grasses with inner hollowness and outer solidity, as well as creepers and medicinal plants with inner pith.

osajho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text in the vocative plural variant osajho, addressed in the praise of mountains and herbs, where the commentary glosses it with antosāraosadhiyo. There may be sandhi or alternation of osadhi + ja (ja from jan), but the form is fixed as osajjha.
osajho.example_1: 316. ‘‘ Tiṇā latāni osajho, pabbatāni vanāni ca;
osajho.translation_1: 316. ‘‘ Hail to grasses, creepers, and herbs, to mountains and forests—
osajho.example_2: Tiṇā latāni osajhoti antopheggubahisāratiṇāni ca latāni ca antosāraosadhiyo ca.
osajho.translation_2: Tiṇā latāni osajho means grasses with inner hollowness and outer solidity, as well as creepers and medicinal plants with inner pith.

indīvarīsāmaṃ.meaning_2: dark as a blue lotus; resembling a blue water lily
indīvarīsāmaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound describing the night (rattiṃ). Accusative singular in the verse. The PEU splits it as indīvarī + sama; some read indīvara + samā. The final -aṃ is the feminine accusative ending.
indīvarīsāmaṃ.translation_1: 317. ‘‘ Hail to the night, dark as a blue lotus, bedecked with stars—

sambulāya.example_1: Tadā hi sotthiseno sambulāya ciramānāya ‘‘ itthiyo nāma lolā, paccāmittampi me gahetvā āgaccheyyā ’’ ti parisaṅkanto paṇṇasālato nikkhamitvā gacchantaraṃ pavisitvā nisīdi.
sambulāya.translation_1: Indeed, at that time, as Sambulā delayed, Sotthisena, suspecting, 'Women are indeed fickle; she might even come back with an enemy of mine,' left the leaf-hut, entered a thicket, and sat down.
sambulāya.example_2: Sotthisenopi sambulāya aggamahesiṭṭhānamattameva adāsi, na punassā koci sakkāro ahosi, atthibhāvampissā na aññāsi, aññāheva itthīhi saddhiṃ abhirami.
sambulāya.translation_2: Sotthisena, for his part, gave Sambulā only the position of chief queen; no further honor was shown to her. He did not even acknowledge her existence and took pleasure only with other women.

osajhoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Unresolvable without context: probably osadha + iti (medicine, thus), the -a elided before -iti; less likely a misreading of a verb form.

indīvarīsāmanti.meaning_2: like a blue lotus; resembling a blue water lily
indīvarīsāmanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is the quotation particle, not part of the word; the entry is for indīvarīsāma. Describes a gesture (ākāra) compared to a blue lotus. Compound of indīvarī (blue water lily, fem) + sāma (like, similar).

indīvarīpupphasamānavaṇṇaṃ.meaning_2: of the colour of a blue lotus flower; with a complexion like a blue water-lily blossom
indīvarīpupphasamānavaṇṇaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text as indīvarīpupphasamānavaṇṇaṃ; accusative singular agreeing with the person described. The first member is indīvarī (blue water-lily), not indīvara.
indīvarīpupphasamānavaṇṇaṃ.translation_1: Indīvarīsāmaṃ means having a color similar to a blue lotus flower.

tumhaṃmhīti.meaning_2: in you; in yourself (thus); you are in it (thus)
tumhaṃmhīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] No sentences supplied; word looks like iti added to a form of tumhaṃmhi, a locative of tumha. Parsed as sandhi of tumhaṃmhi + iti. Cannot be confirmed without context.

abhisiñcāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be consecrated; having had (someone) anointed as king/queen
abhisiñcāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of abhisiñcāpeti (causative of abhisiñcati, 'sprinkles over, consecrates'). Used of anointing a king (sotthisenassa) and a chief queen (sambulaṃ) in the text.
abhisiñcāpetvā.example_1: Evaṃ vatvā mahāsatto tattheva taṃ abhisiñcāpetvā nagaraṃ pāhesi.
abhisiñcāpetvā.translation_1: Having spoken thus, the Great Being had him consecrated right there and sent him to the city.
abhisiñcāpetvā.example_2: Rājā tesaṃ āgatabhāvaṃ ñatvā uyyānaṃ gantvā tattheva sotthisenassa chattaṃ ussāpetvā sambulaṃ aggamahesiṭṭhāne abhisiñcāpetvā nagaraṃ pavesetvā sayaṃ isipabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā uyyāne vāsaṃ kappesi, rājanivesaneyeva ca nibaddhaṃ bhuñji.
abhisiñcāpetvā.translation_2: The king, having learned of their arrival, went to the park and right there had the royal umbrella raised over Sotthisena. He had Sambulā consecrated in the position of chief queen and, having brought them into the city, he himself went forth into the ascetic life and took up residence in the park, but he always ate in the royal palace itself.

upaṇḍupaṇḍukajātā.meaning_2: extremely pale; very pale in appearance
upaṇḍupaṇḍukajātā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes Sambulā in the text; nominative singular. The first element is intensive upa + paṇḍu (pale).
upaṇḍupaṇḍukajātā.example_1: Sambulā sapattidosavasena kisā ahosi upaṇḍupaṇḍukajātā dhamanīsanthatagattā.
upaṇḍupaṇḍukajātā.translation_1: Sambulā, due to the jealousy caused by her rivals, became thin, very pale, and her body was covered with visible veins.

vimānaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the text ('should disrespect'), from vi + √man with the causative sign. The PEU splits it as vi + māna + ṇaya + eyya. Verb form of vimāneti, in optative; cf. the paired sammānaye.
vimānaye.example_1: Sammānaye maṃ na ca maṃ vimānaye, itopi me tāta tato varaṃ siyā.
vimānaye.translation_1: If he would honor me and not disrespect me, then dear father, even that (life in the forest) would be better for me than this (life here).

anāḷhīyāti.meaning_2: not distressful; not troubled; free from affliction
anāḷhīyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a negative adjective from āḷhīya (troubled, distressed); the final -ti looks like a quotation particle, so the entry is for anāḷhīya alone. Doubtful reading.

anāḷhā.meaning_2: without support; without a bolster; poor
anāḷhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Gloss in the text for anāḷhīyā. Perhaps na + āḷhiya, so the reading anāḷhā may stand for anāḷhiyā; feminine nominative singular.

sotthisena.meaning_2: Sotthisena; name of a king (son of the ascetic in the Jātaka story)
sotthisena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a king, vocative singular in the text. The compound is sotthi (well-being) + senā (army), with the final -ā shortened before the -a suffix; the PEU also suggests this split.
sotthisena.example_1: Evaṃ tāya attano parisussanakāraṇe tāpasassa kathite tāpaso rājānaṃ pakkosāpetvā ‘‘ tāta, sotthisena tayi kuṭṭharogābhibhūte araññaṃ pavisante tayā saddhiṃ pavisitvā taṃ upaṭṭhahantī attano saccabalena tava rogaṃ vūpasametvā yā te rajje patiṭṭhānakāraṇamakāsi, tassā nāma tvaṃ neva ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ, na nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ jānāsi, ayuttaṃ te kataṃ, mittadubbhikammaṃ nāmetaṃ pāpakan ’’ ti vatvā puttaṃ ovadanto gāthamāha –
sotthisena.translation_1: Thus, when the cause of her wasting away was told by her to the ascetic, the ascetic, having sent for the king, said, ‘Dear Sotthisena, when you were overcome by leprosy and entered the wilderness, she entered with you and respectfully attended to you. By her own power of truth, she assuaged your disease, and she was the cause of your establishment in the kingdom. But you, indeed, do not know her standing place or her sitting place. You have done what is improper. This act of treachery is indeed evil,’ and admonishing his son, he uttered the verse:

sambulāyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name; -yāti is the quotative particle (sambulā iti) appended to the word in the text.

madāti.meaning_2: is intoxicated; is proud; is infatuated
madāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text madāti is likely madati with -ā- for the metre or sandhi. 3rd singular present.

dubbalacakkhūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound used as a vocative in the verse; the final -si is the sandhi of -si (2nd sg. pronoun) rather than part of the word. Some analyses read the form as dubbalacakkhuka.
dubbalacakkhūsi.example_1: 344. ‘‘ Jiṇṇo dubbalacakkhūsi, na rūpaṃ sādhu passasi;
dubbalacakkhūsi.translation_1: 344. ‘You are old and weak-sighted; you do not see forms clearly.

tuṇḍiyā.meaning_2: robber; plunderer; one who extracts taxes by force
tuṇḍiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural, glossed by the commentary as adhammena balisādhakā, unlawful tax collectors who oppress people. The PEU suggests derivation from tuṇḍa with -ika/-iya.
tuṇḍiyā.example_1: 346. ‘‘ Rattiñhi corā khādanti, divā khādanti tuṇḍiyā;
tuṇḍiyā.translation_1: 346. ‘Indeed, at night robbers plunder, by day royal officers plunder.
tuṇḍiyā.translation_2: Tuṇḍiyā refers to those who collect taxes unlawfully, oppressing others by killing, binding, and so on.

nillenakāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural of nillenaka. The PEU suggests nillenaka = ni + līna + ka. Here probably the plural of nillenakaṃ. The form ends in -āni, so the lemma might better be nillenaka. The commentary glosses it as a place to hide.
nillenakāni.example_1: Nillenakāni kubbanti, vane āhatva kaṇṭakan ’’ ti.
nillenakāni.translation_1: They make hiding places, having brought thorns into the forest.’

tuṇḍiyāti.meaning_2: of Tuṇḍiya; so Tuṇḍiya (said); Tuṇḍiya indeed
tuṇḍiyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably tuṇḍiyā (oblique of the proper name Tuṇḍiya) plus the quotation particle ti. The PEU lists tuṇḍiya as a noun meaning robber or rebel. If it is not a quotation but an enclitic, the entry would be tuṇḍiya, masc, meaning name of a robber.

nillenakānīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is joined with iti (-iti), the sandhi of the quotation marker, so the entry is for the bare word nillena kaṃ with the -ti cut off. Analysis na + liena + ka is not confirmed; compare the reading of the commentary, which may also be read as ni + lena + ka, 'without shelter', or ni+layana. The second element is unclear. The accusative singular with -ti marks a quoted word.

sāliyabalibaddo.meaning_2: the bull Sāliya; the ox named Sāliya
sāliyabalibaddo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a bull (balibaddha) in the Jātaka story. Nominative singular in the text.
sāliyabalibaddo.example_1: Tattha yathāti yathā ayaṃ vedanāppatto sāliyabalibaddo seti, evaṃ sayatūti attho.
sāliyabalibaddo.translation_1: Here, yathā means: “Just as this bull Sāliya, overcome by pain, lies, so may he lie down.”

aṭanakāti.meaning_2: used to run; given to wandering
aṭanakāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] -ti is a quotation ending (aṭanakā + iti); lemma probably aṭanaka. Vowel shortening of -yu- to -ana- is uncertain; some editions read aṭanakā.

viputto.meaning_2: childless; bereft of children; without a son
viputto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text nominative singular used of Pañcāla, glossed by the commentary as without a son; another analysis takes vi- as 'separated from'.
viputto.translation_1: 362. ‘May Pañcāla thus wail, childless, may he pine away,

viputtā.meaning_2: deprived of a calf; separated from a calf; bereft of a son
viputtā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular feminine, agreeing with gāvī: viputtā gāvī, 'a cow deprived of her calf'. The prefix vi- here has a separative sense.
viputtā.example_1: Yathāyaṃ kapaṇā gāvī, viputtā paridhāvatī ’’ ti.
viputtā.translation_1: Just as this wretched cow runs about, deprived of her calf.”

khīrapā.meaning_2: milk-drinking; suckling; (of a calf) that drinks its mother's milk
khīrapā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text khīrapā is masculine nominative singular agreeing with vacchako (calves); the commentary glosses it khīrapako vacchako. Some editions/analyses take it as a compound with √pā (khīra + pā, 'milk-drinking'), but the commentary's khīrapaka with suffix -pa supports the form khīrapa.
khīrapā.example_1: Kathaṃ no asikosatthā, khīrapā haññate pajā ’’ ti.
khīrapā.translation_1: How indeed is the milk-drinking calf killed for a sword-sheath?”’
khīrapā.example_2: Khīrapā haññate pajāti pāparājassa sevakehi khīrapako vacchako haññati, idāni sā dhenu puttasokena paridevati, sopi rājā ayaṃ dhenu viya paridevatūti rājānaṃ akkosiṃsuyeva.
khīrapā.translation_2: Khīrapā haññate pajā means: the milk-drinking calf is killed by the evil king’s servants. Now that cow laments by grief for its son. They indeed cursed the king, saying: ‘May that king also lament like this cow!’

surajjakanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed from su + rajja + ka (PEU gives su + rajja + ka). In the text it is the accusative singular surajjakanti = surajjakaṃ + iti, with -ṃ assimilated to -n before the quotation particle. A doubtful or conjectural reading; the context is missing.

jayaddisa.meaning_2: Jayaddisa; name of a king (and previous birth of the Buddha); conqueror of the enemy
jayaddisa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name occurring in a list of past births. The PEU analysis jaya + disa is doubtful; the second element may be disā (direction) or a name-formation rather than a verbal derivative.
jayaddisa.example_1: Kiṃchanda kumbha jayaddisa chaddanta, atha paṇḍitasambhava sirakapi;
jayaddisa.translation_1: Kiṃchanda, Kumbha, Jayaddisa, Chaddanta; then Paṇḍitasambhava, Sirakapi;

sambula.meaning_2: Sambula (name of a man; name of a queen; name of a story)
sambula.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. In the text it is nominative singular in a list of names. The PEU suggests a possible connection with sambhu and sambuka, but the name's derivation is uncertain.
sambula.translation_1: Dakarakkhasa, Paṇḍaranāgavara; then Sambula, Tindukadeva’s son.”

mahāpatāpano.meaning_2: Mahāpatāpana; name of a king in the Cūḷadhammapāla Jātaka
mahāpatāpano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. Nominative singular in the text. PEU suggests mahanta + patāpana; the first element is probably mahā-.
mahāpatāpano.example_1: Cūḷadhammapālajātakasmiñhi mahāpatāpano nāma rājā puttaṃ ghātetvā puttasokena hadayena phalitena matāya deviyā sayampi deviṃ anusocanto hadayena phaliteneva mari.
mahāpatāpano.translation_1: Indeed, in the Cūḷadhammapāla Jātaka, a king named Mahāpatāpana, having killed his son, and with the queen having died of a broken heart due to grief for her son, he himself, grieving for the queen, also died with a broken heart.

ucchijjitvā.meaning_2: having been utterly destroyed; having been cut off; having been annihilated
ucchijjitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive absolutive. In the text it agrees in sense with raṭṭha, 'together with his kingdom, having been utterly destroyed'. The simplex chijjitvā is more common; the ud- prefix adds the sense of complete destruction.
ucchijjitvā.example_1: Imasmiṃ panatthe sarabhaṅgajātake (jā.2.17.50 ādayo) purohitassa vacanaṃ gahetvā daṇḍakirañño kisavacche aparajjhitvā saha raṭṭhena ucchijjitvā kukkuḷaniraye nibbattabhāvo ca mātaṅgajātake (jā.1.15.1 ādayo) majjharañño brāhmaṇānaṃ kathaṃ gahetvā mātaṅgatāpase aparajjhitvā saha raṭṭhena ucchijjitvā niraye nibbattabhāvo ca ghaṭapaṇḍitajātake (jā.1.10.165 ādayo) dasabhātikarājadārakānaṃ mohamūḷhānaṃ vacanaṃ gahetvā kaṇhadīpāyane aparajjhitvā vāsudevakulassa nāsitabhāvo ca kathetabbo.
ucchijjitvā.translation_1: In this regard, the following should be recounted: how, in the Sarabhaṅga Jātaka (Jā.2.17.50 ff.), King Daṇḍaki, having taken the purohita’s word, offended against Kisavaccha, and together with his kingdom, was utterly destroyed and reborn in Kukkula Hell; and how, in the Mātaṅga Jātaka (Jā.1.15.1 ff.), King Majjha, having taken the brahmins’ word, offended against the ascetic Mātaṅga, and together with his kingdom, was utterly destroyed and reborn in hell; and how, in the Ghaṭapaṇḍita Jātaka (Jā.1.10.165 ff.), the Vāsudeva clan was destroyed after the ten deluded royal brother princes took the word of Kaṇhadīpāyana and offended against him.

bhañjanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the predicate noun of kāḷakaṇṇī ('Misfortune' personified), in the nominative singular: 'destroyer of the wheel of merit'. The -yu/-ī suffix forms a feminine agent noun; the PEU entry gives the same analysis, though the meaning here is more 'one who destroys' than 'a woman who breaks'.
bhañjanī.example_1: Evaṃ sā kāḷakaṇṇī, mahārāja, ramati patirūpadesavāsādino kusalacakkassa bhañjanī.
bhañjanī.translation_1: Thus, O Great King, that Misfortune, the destroyer of the wheel of merit, delights in the suitable region for dwelling and so on.

upajīvitabbā.grammar: pr, caus of jīvati; ptp of upajīvati
upajīvitabbā.meaning_2: to be dependent on; to subsist on; to be supported by
upajīvitabbā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the potential participle upajīvitabbā (masculine nominative plural), used in a gloss explaining sājīvā as 'to be subsisted together'.
upajīvitabbā.translation_1: Sājīvā honti means having a similar livelihood and being mutually supported.

iṇadānañca.meaning_2: lending money; giving a loan; debt settlement
iṇadānañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text -ñca is the sandhi of iṇadānaṃ + ca; accusative singular. Compound of iṇa (debt) + dāna (giving).
iṇadānañca.translation_1: One should not make [decisions concerning] treasure or lending money by relying on others.”
iṇadānañca.translation_2: The hidden treasure and the debts, he said this to Punṇaka.

kodhasā.meaning_2: because of anger; out of anger; by anger
kodhasā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Dative-ablative of kodha with suffix -(a)sā (cf. Sanskrit krodhasā), used as an adverbial in Jātaka verse and commentary; commentary glosses kodhena.
kodhasā.example_1: Kodhasā hi bahū phītā, kulā akulataṃ gatā.
kodhasā.translation_1: Indeed, by anger, many prosperous families have gone to ruin.”
kodhasā.example_2: Kodhasā hīti, tāta, kodhena hi bahūni phītāni rājakulāni akulabhāvaṃ gatāni mahāvināsameva pattānīti.
kodhasā.translation_2: Kodhasā hī: “Dear child, indeed, by anger, many prosperous royal families have gone to ruin and have attained great ruin indeed.”

ajutakare.meaning_2: not practising crookedness; not behaving deceitfully; not a cheat
ajutakare.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Explained in the commentary by akkha-ajutānaṃ akaraṇasīla. Locative singular in the text.
ajutakare.example_1: Anakkhākitaveti anakkhe akitave ajutakare ceva akerāṭike ca.
ajutakare.translation_1: Anakkhākitave: [Those who are] without gambling, without deceit, not gamblers, and not crooked.

yañcevāti.meaning_2: and just whatever; and this very thing; and so it is
yañcevāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi string, probably yaṃ + ca + eva + iti or yaṃ + ce + eva + iti. Segmentation uncertain; the final -ti is the quotative iti, and the whole may be split further (yaṃ + ceva + iti). No sentence is given.

subāḷhamadhikopitanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form in the text is a sandhi of subāḷhaṃ with adhikopitanti? The text reads subāḷham-adhiko-pita? Unclear; treated here as su + bāḷhaṃ (adverb).

otārayi.meaning_2: made (someone) fall (into); caused to descend (into); made go down (into)
otārayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative aorist 3rd singular; in the text contrasted with patārayi. Commentarial gloss of ava + √tar, 'to cause to go down'.
otārayi.example_1: Mā , tāta , issaromhīti , anatthāya patārayīti, tāta,‘‘ ahaṃ pathavissaro ’’ ti mā mahājanaṃ kāyaduccaritādianatthāya patārayi mā otārayi, yathā taṃ anatthaṃ samādāya vattati, mā evamakāsīti attho.
otārayi.translation_1: Mā, tāta, issaromhīti, anatthāya patārayī: “Dear child, thinking, ‘I am lord of the earth,’ do not lead the multitude of people astray for the harm of bodily misconduct and so on; do not cause them to fall into it. Do not do it in such a way as one conducts oneself undertaking that harm. This is the meaning.”

abhijaccabalañceva.meaning_2: and the strength of noble birth
abhijaccabalañceva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of abhijaccabalaṃ (nominative singular of abhijaccabala, 'strength of noble birth') with ceva (ca + eva). Part of a verse listing strengths; sandhi -ṃ + c → -ñc.
abhijaccabalañceva.translation_1: 29. ‘‘ And the strength of noble birth, that is certainly the fourth;

abhijaccabalanti.meaning_2: strength of noble birth; power of high lineage
abhijaccabalanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text form is abhijaccabalanti = abhijaccabalaṃ + iti, with nasal assimilation before -ti. Abhijacca is an adjective meaning 'of noble birth'.

paññātiādimāha.meaning_2: and he said (beginning with) 'as is known'; and he spoke thus beginning with 'is known'
paññātiādimāha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution uncertain: possibly paññāti + ādim + āha, or paññā + ti + ādim + āha. Final element is āha, the perfect/aorist of brūti or vac. No sentence given in the text, so the exact division is a guess.

pothiyamānāpi.meaning_2: being beaten; being struck; being tortured
pothiyamānāpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of pothiyati (to beat, strike). In the text compounded with api: pothiyamānāpi = pothiyamānā + api, nominative plural. The PEU analysis as a future passive participle (ptp) is possible but the form here is present participle.
pothiyamānāpi.example_1: ‘‘ ime mayā pothiyamānāpi mayhaṃ yevatthāya paridevanti, ayuttaṃ kammaṃ karomī ’’ ti.
pothiyamānāpi.translation_1: “Even though these are being beaten by me, they lament only for my good. I am doing an improper action.”

yevatthāya.meaning_2: just for this purpose; only for this sake; for this very reason
yevatthāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of emphatic yeva with dative atthāya (for the sake of). In the sentence: 'they lament solely for my sake'. Could also be analysed as ye + va + atthāya, but the emphatic yeva fits best.
yevatthāya.example_1: ‘‘ ime mayā pothiyamānāpi mayhaṃ yevatthāya paridevanti, ayuttaṃ kammaṃ karomī ’’ ti.
yevatthāya.translation_1: “Even though these are being beaten by me, they lament only for my good. I am doing an improper action.”

moggallānaāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the proper name Moggallāna and the quotative ti/āti. So the word as it stands is treated as a sandhi compound, not as a single noun.

uppaṇhāhīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person singular imperative, with the quotation particle -ti attached; the entry is for the verb form only. The analysis is uncertain: possibly from uppaṇhāti, causative of the root √ghar (burn, be hot).

jotipola.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of jotipāla, possibly dialectal or scribal; vocative singular in the text. Compound of joti + pāla, 'guardian of light', name of Mahāgovinda.
jotipola.example_1: Athassa ācariyo tussitvā attano santakaṃ khaggaratanaṃ sandhiyuttaṃ meṇḍakasiṅgadhanuṃ sandhiyuttaṃ tūṇīraṃ attano sannāhakañcukaṃ uṇhīsañca datvā ‘‘ tāta jotipola, ahaṃ mahallako, idāni tvaṃ ime māṇavake sikkhāpehī ’’ ti pañcasatamāṇavakepi tasseva niyyādesi.
jotipola.translation_1: Then his teacher, having been pleased, gave him his own sword-jewel, a deftly joined ram's-horn bow, a deftly joined quiver, his own coat of mail, and a turban, and said, “Dear Jotipāla, I am an aged elder; now you teach these pupils.” He then entrusted even five hundred pupils to him.

seḷento.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle seḷento, masculine nominative singular, in a list of sounds (shouting, roaring, etc.). Probably a contraction or alternative form of siloketi.
seḷento.example_1: Mahājano unnādento vagganto apphoṭento seḷento accharaṃ paharanto mahākolāhalaṃ katvā vatthābharaṇādīni khipi.
seḷento.translation_1: The great mass of people, making (the place) resound, shouting, clapping their hands, proclaiming, and striking a finger-snap, made a great uproar and cast off their clothes and ornaments etc.
seḷento.example_2: Atha so sakkassa devarañño paricārikaṃ viya taṃ attano paricārikaṃ disvā khattiyamānaṃ uppādetvā ‘‘ mayi kira dharamāneyeva mama bhariyaṃ aññe gahetvā gamissantī ’’ ti sīho viya rājaṅgaṇe vijambhamāno ‘‘ sakalanagaravāsino me āgatabhāvaṃ jānantū ’’ ti vagganto nadanto seḷento apphoṭento ‘‘ idāni te jīvaggāhaṃ gahessāmi, rathādayo me yojentū ’’ ti anantaraṃ gāthamāha –
seḷento.translation_2: Then King Kusa, seeing her, his own attendant, as if she were an attendant of Sakka, the king of devas, aroused his khattiya pride. “While I am still alive, will others indeed come and take my wife?” he thought. Like a lion, displaying his majesty in the royal courtyard, he shouted, roared, whistled, and clapped his hands, saying, “Let all city dwellers know of my arrival! Now I will capture them alive; let them yoke my chariots and so forth!” Immediately after, he uttered the verse:

kalappacullakanigamaṃ.meaning_2: village of Kalappacullaka; the village named Kalappacullaka
kalappacullakanigamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. A place name, the village near which Sālissara is told to settle with the ascetics.
kalappacullakanigamaṃ.example_1: Atha mahāsatto sālissaraṃ āmantetvā ‘‘ sālissara, ayaṃ assamo isigaṇassa nappahoti, tvaṃ imaṃ isigaṇaṃ gahetvā majjharañño vijite kalappacullakanigamaṃ upanissāya vasāhī ’’ ti āha.
kalappacullakanigamaṃ.translation_1: Then the Great Being addressed Sālissara, saying, “Sālissara, this hermitage is not sufficient for the company of ascetics. Taking this company of ascetics, go and dwell relying on the Kalappacullaka village in the realm of King Majjha.”

meṇḍissara.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of an ascetic addressed by the Bodhisatta and sent with the company of ascetics to the Sātodikā river. Accusative singular in the text; also vocative in direct address.
meṇḍissara.example_1: Bodhisatto meṇḍissaraṃ āmantetvā,‘‘ meṇḍissara, tvaṃ imaṃ isigaṇaṃ ādāya suraṭṭhajanapadassa sīmantare sātodikā nāma nadī atthi, tassā tīre vasāhī ’’ ti uyyojesi, puna kapiṭṭhakaassamo paripūri.
meṇḍissara.translation_1: The Bodhisatta addressed Meṇḍissara, saying, “Meṇḍissara, taking this company of ascetics, dwell on the bank of the Sātodikā River, which is located in the border region of Suraṭṭha country.” He dismissed him, and again the Kapiṭṭhaka hermitage was filled.

āvusā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative form of address to an equal or junior; here āvusā is a variant spelling used in the Jātaka prose. Often used by senior monks addressing juniors.
āvusā.example_1: Āvusā mayhaṃ manopadoso natthi, devatā pana kupitā ito sattame divase sakalaraṭṭhaṃ araṭṭhaṃ karissanti, tvaṃ puttadāraṃ gahetvā sīghaṃ palāyitvā aññattha yāhīti.
āvusā.translation_1: “Friend, there is no mental corruption in me. But the devas are angered; from this day, on the seventh day, they will destroy the entire kingdom. You, taking your children and wife, quickly flee elsewhere!”

vanakīḷādīnaṃ.meaning_2: forest game; amusement in the forest
vanakīḷādīnaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive plural in -ānaṃ in the text, in vanakīḷādīnaṃ ('forest games and so on'). Part of a compound with ādi.
vanakīḷādīnaṃ.example_1: Susaññatānaṃ isīnanti, bhante, na mayaṃ vanakīḷādīnaṃ atthāya āgatā, atha kho kāyādīhi susaññatānaṃ sīlasampannānaṃ isīnaṃ dassanatthāya idhāgatā.
vanakīḷādīnaṃ.translation_1: Susaññatānaṃ isīnaṃ means “Venerable sir, we have not come for the purpose of forest games and so on, but rather we have come here for the purpose of seeing the sages who are well-restrained in body and so on, and who are endowed with virtue.” (susaññatānaṃ isīnaṃ)

emha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person plural aorist of eti, joined here as pucchitāyemha = pucchitāya + emha in sandhi. The related entry takes it as ā + i + mha. In the sentence it means 'we have come (to ask)'.
emha.example_1: Pucchitāyemha pañheti sarabhaṅgasatthāraṃ pañhe pucchituṃ emha, āgatāmhāti attho.
emha.translation_1: Pucchitāyemha pañhe means “we have come to ask Teacher Sarabhaṅga questions; this is the meaning.” (pucchitāyemha pañhe)

nevāti.meaning_2: not so; it is not thus; neither... nor
nevāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + eva + iti (or na eva + iti), quoted particle. No sentence given; analysis uncertain but the form is most naturally resolved this way.

raññanti.meaning_2: to the king, and; for the king, and; kings' ... and
raññanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of raññaṃ (dative/genitive singular of rāja) + anti, the enclitic form of iti. Sometimes also raññaṃ + ti; the PEU entry treats raññaṃ alone as 'to kings'. Uncertain.

yañcāsi.meaning_2: which you desired; which you wished for
yañcāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ (relative pronoun, accusative singular) + āsi (aorist 2nd singular of atthi, 'you were'). In the text: 'yaṃ āsi abhipatthitaṃ' = 'which you had desired'. Alternative split yaṃ + asi (2nd sg. of √as 1) is also possible.
yañcāsi.translation_1: asked the first question, which he had desired.

yañcāsīti.meaning_2: and whatever (he) approached; and that which (he) went to
yañcāsīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ, ca, āsi (aorist of atthi/√as, 'was') and the quotative iti; the final -cā- is ca + ā-. No sentence context available, so the analysis is uncertain.

titikkhituṃ.meaning_2: to endure; to bear; to be patient (with)
titikkhituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive used with sakkā: 'it is possible to endure'. The PEU analysis (tija + kha + tuṃ) suggests the root √tij; the form is of the titikkhati type (cf. khama).
titikkhituṃ.example_1: 65. ‘‘ Sakkā ubhinnaṃ vacanaṃ titikkhituṃ, sadisassa vā seṭṭhatarassa vāpi;
titikkhituṃ.translation_1: 65. “It is possible to endure the word of both (ubhinnaṃ), of an equal or even of a superior;

veravūpasamanippaṭighasabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ.meaning_2: characterized by the appeasement of enmity and the absence of anger; called the state of enmity being stilled and free from ill will
veravūpasamanippaṭighasabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Long bahubbīhi compound qualifying atthaṃ; accusative singular in the text. The parts are vera (enmity), vūpasama (appeasement), nippaṭigha (without ill will), sabhāva (nature), saṅkhāta (called, characterized).
veravūpasamanippaṭighasabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ.translation_1: Herein, `this matter` (etamatthaṃ) refers to this benefit characterized by the appeasement of enmities and the absence of anger.

paripūrāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be filled; having filled
paripūrāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive; in the text with cāṭiyo, 'having had the pots filled'. Sometimes analysed as a direct absolutive of paripūreti with the same sense.
paripūrāpetvā.example_1: So tassa kujjhitvā ‘‘ ayaṃ kūṭajaṭilo ettakaṃ kālaṃ nāgarānaṃ santike mamaññeva aguṇaṃ kathesi maññe, hotu jānissāmī ’’ ti cintetvā ‘‘ sve amhākaṃ gharadvāraṃ āgaccheyyāthā ’’ ti nimantetvā punadivase purāṇagūthassa cāṭiyo paripūrāpetvā tāpasesu āgatesu tesaṃ bhikkhābhājanāni gūthassa pūrāpetvā dvāraṃ pidahāpetvā musalāni ca lohadaṇḍe ca gāhāpetvā isīnaṃ sīsāni bhindāpetvā jaṭāsu gāhāpetvā kaḍḍhāpetvā sunakhehi khādāpetvā tattheva bhinnaṃ pathaviṃ pavisitvā sunakhamahāniraye nibbattati, tatrassa tigāvutappamāṇasarīraṃ ahosi.
paripūrāpetvā.translation_1: He, having become angry with him, thought, “This matted-hair cheat has, for so long, only spoken of my lack of virtue in the vicinity of the citizens, I suppose. Let it be, I will know (what to do to him)!” and having invited him, saying, “May you come to our house door tomorrow,” on the next day, having caused pots to be filled with old feces, when the ascetics arrived, he caused their alms bowls to be filled with feces, had the door closed, had pestles and iron clubs taken, had the heads of the sages broken, had them grabbed by their matted hair, had them dragged, had them eaten by dogs, and right there, having entered the split earth, he was reborn in the great dog hell, where his body was three gāvutas in size.

parigalitvā.meaning_2: having slipped down; having slid down; having slipped off
parigalitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive from pari + √gal 1 (drip, flow), used of slipping or sliding down after losing footing. In both sentences it precedes the main verb patati / āsādetvā kālamakāsi.
parigalitvā.example_1: So parigalitvā patanto matthakena khadirakhāṇukaṃ āsādetvā sūlaggeyeva kālamakāsi.
parigalitvā.translation_1: He, slipping down and falling, struck an acacia stump with his head and died right on the tip of a stake.
parigalitvā.example_2: Pabbatamatthake ṭhitakāle vāto paharati, so vātappahārena parigalitvā patati.
parigalitvā.translation_2: When he stands on the mountain top, the wind strikes him, and he, slipping down by the striking of the wind, falls.

ākaḍḍhāpetvā.meaning_2: causes to be dragged; has (someone) dragged
ākaḍḍhāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of ākaḍḍhati; absolutive in the text with -tvā. The string under the prefix ā appears as ākaḍḍhāpetvā.
ākaḍḍhāpetvā.example_1: Tathā chedāpetvā dvīhi kasāhi pahārasahassehi tāḷāpetvā jaṭāsu gahetvā ākaḍḍhāpetvā paṭikujjaṃ nipajjāpetvā piṭṭhiyaṃ paṇhiyā paharitvā mahādukkhasamappitaṃ akāsi.
ākaḍḍhāpetvā.translation_1: Thus, he caused him to be cut off, had him beaten with two whips with a thousand blows, taking him by his matted hair, had him dragged, had him laid down face down, struck him on the back with his heel, and subjected him to great suffering.

abhicintento.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle masculine nominative singular in the text (manasā abhicintento). Forms from the causative abhicinteti; the PEU entry connects it to cinta.
abhicintento.example_1: Manasābhicintayanti manasā abhicintento atthaṃ paṭivijjhitvā candasahassaṃ sūriyasahassaṃ uṭṭhāpento viya pākaṭaṃ katvā yo kathetuṃ sakkotīti attho.
abhicintento.translation_1: Manasābhicintayaṃ means one who, reflecting mentally, penetrates the meaning and makes it clear as if causing a thousand moons and a thousand suns to rise, and is able to explain—that is the meaning.

piḷitāpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text piḷitā pi is sandhi; the entry is for the participle alone. Nominative plural agreeing with santā. The PEU analysis piḷa + ta and √pīḷ fit.
piḷitāpi.example_1: Dukkhena phuṭṭhā piḷitāpi santā, chandā dosā ca na jahanti dhamman ’’ ti.
piḷitāpi.translation_1: Even when afflicted and touched by suffering, good people do not abandon good principles through desire or hatred.”

vatrassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vatrassa is genitive singular of vattra, meaning 'of the asura named Vatra'. Variant spelling of vatra; the compound vatrabhū occurs alongside.
vatrassa.translation_1: Vatrabhū means the overcomer of the asura named Vatra.

purisapalobhinipāricariyaṃ.meaning_2: service of seducing men; attendance on men in a seductive way
purisapalobhinipāricariyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The compound may be analysed as purisapalobhinī + pāricariyā; the form palobhini- is a sandhi variant of palobhinī before p-.
purisapalobhinipāricariyaṃ.example_1: Tattha pumaṃ gatāti purisaṃ upasaṅkamantā samānā purisapalobhinipāricariyaṃ na jānanti.
purisapalobhinipāricariyaṃ.translation_1: Here, having approached a man (pumaṃ gatā) means that, being those who approach a man, they do not know the ministration of seducing men.

haṃsayeti.meaning_2: causes to sound; makes (a swan) cry; imitates the call of a swan
haṃsayeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only the compound haṃsayoni appears in the given entry; haṃsayeti itself is not attested in the supplied sentences. Formally a causative of √haṃs (rise; elate), here perhaps 'makes a swan sound'. 3rd singular present.

āsādituṃ.meaning_2: to entice; to approach; to assail
āsādituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive, glossed in the text by āsāduṃ; the commentary treats it as meaning 'to entice'. Possibly related to āsādeti (approach; assail).

missituṃ.meaning_2: to mingle (with); to mix (with); to associate (with)
missituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of misseti (missayati); here with kilesena, 'to mingle with Isisiṅga by means of defilement'.
missituṃ.example_1: Tattha pakkāmīti tena hi, devarāja, āvajjeyyāsi manti attano sayanagabbhaṃ pavisitvā alaṅkaritvā isisiṅgaṃ kilesena missituṃ icchantī pakkāmi, bhikkhave, sā accharā tassa assamaṃ gatāti.
missituṃ.translation_1: Here, departed (pakkāmī) means: ‘Then, King of Devas, you should consider me!’ Having said this, desiring to mingle with Isisiṅga by means of defilement, she entered her own sleeping chamber, adorned herself, and then departed. Mendicants, that nymph went to his hermitage.

urajā.meaning_2: born from the breast; breast-born; grown on the breast
urajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural in the text (jātā urajā). Describing water-lilies in the Jātaka verses: some 'breast-born', i.e. growing out of the water on stems from the breast of the pond. Sometimes analysed as ura + √jan + kvi.

duvijā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative plural in the verse (duvijā nelasambhūtā, referring to teeth); the gloss explains duvijā as dvijā. Also an epithet of brahmins and birds.
duvijā.translation_1: your teeth, twice-born, grown in faultless gums, are beautiful.

duvijāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a compound of du (two) + vijāti (birth); the related PEU entry duvijāta suggests a variant reading in -a. Stands for a twice-born person; no sentence supplied.

jiñjūkaphalasannibhāti.meaning_2: like a jiñjūka fruit; resembling a jiñjūka fruit
jiñjūkaphalasannibhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of jiñjūkaphalasannibhā (adj, 'like a jiñjūka fruit') with the quotation particle iti. The final ā + i becomes āti.

jīvanakasatte.meaning_2: living being; creature that makes a living
jīvanakasatte.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text, agreeing with jīvanakasatte. Compound of jīvanaka (living, making a living) + satta (being).
jīvanakasatte.example_1: Kasigorakkhāti iminā kasiñca gorakkhañca nissāya jīvanakasatte dasseti.
jīvanakasatte.translation_1: Those who live by farming and cattle-rearing means, by this, it shows living beings who subsist by relying on farming and cattle-rearing.

vitthārīkatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominal compound with kata; used absolutely/elliptically in the sentence ("having been expanded"). Perhaps better analysed as vitthāra + kata with -ī- before the consonant cluster.
vitthārīkatā.example_1: Parakkantanti yattakaṃ isīnaṃ parakkantaṃ, vitthārīkatā imasmiṃ himavante yattakā isayo vasantīti attho.
vitthārīkatā.translation_1: The sphere of activity means whatever the sphere of activity of the sages, the meaning is whatever the extent to which the sages dwell, having expanded their presence, in this Himalayas.

sopavāhanaṃ.meaning_2: with attendants; accompanied by followers; complete with its retinue
sopavāhanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sa + upavāhana (so + upavāhana), meaning saparivāra per the commentary. Describes the couch (pallaṅkaṃ). Accusative singular here; the spelling sovaṇṇaṃ closely preceding is a separate word.
sopavāhanaṃ.translation_1: 125. “He quickly sent a golden couch, complete with its attendants;”

vimado.meaning_2: free from intoxication; free from delusion; without vanity
vimado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentary glosses vimado as nimmado vigatasaññabhāvo, i.e. without mada or unawareness. Nominative singular in the text; also used as the brahmin's name.
vimado.translation_1: 127. “The brahmin, free from delusion, having awoken after three years;”
vimado.translation_2: Vimado (vimado) means free from intoxication, without a state of unconsciousness.

paviloketvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative paviloketi (pa + vi + loketi, 'to look around'); the -ṇe- is the causative sign. Used with samantā in the sentence.
paviloketvā.translation_1: Having looked all around, he shed tears, weeping.

vattayi.meaning_2: shed; caused to flow; let fall; produced
vattayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative vattayati (from √vatt); used with assūni 'tears' in the sense 'shed tears'. The PEU analysis as vattu + ṇaya + ī looks doubtful.
vattayi.translation_1: Having looked all around, he shed tears, weeping.
vattayi.example_2: ‘ Passasanto muhuṃ uṇhaṃ, rudaṃ assūni vattayi.
vattayi.translation_2: ‘ Wept and shed tears, breathing heavily and sighing.

cavite.meaning_2: fallen from; fallen away from; departed from
cavite.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of cavati, modifying jhānā brahmacariyā; locative singular in -e in the text.
cavite.example_1: Tasmiṃ tamhā jhānā brahmacariyā cavite yathā taṃ sakkena patthitaṃ, tatheva ahosi.
cavite.translation_1: When his holy life had fallen from that absorption, just as it had been desired by Sakka, so too it happened.

sopavāhananti.meaning_2: together with attendants; accompanied by followers; with retinue
sopavāhananti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -nti is the quotative ending; the entry is for the compound sopavāhana. Glossed by the commentary as saparivāraṃ.

sahassapaṭiyatthatanti.meaning_2: adorned with a thousand preparations; arrayed with a thousand decorations
sahassapaṭiyatthatanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the word carries the quotation particle -ti; the entry is for the directory form. The PEU analysis (sahassa + paṭaya + atthatha) appears doubtful; it is treated here as a bahubbīhi compound of sahassa + paṭiyattata.

vimadoti.meaning_2: free from pride; without intoxication; without conceit
vimadoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is the quotative particle (iti) and is not part of the word; possibly vimado + ti, or vimadā + ti. In compounds vi- negates mada (pride, intoxication). The PEU entry vimada ('lack of intoxication') supports the analysis vi + mada; the translation 'Vimada' as a proper name is probably a machine error.

sambhutanti.meaning_2: came to be; were; arose; well came to be
sambhutanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word occurs in Jātaka-ṭīkā prose and has the -isuṃ ending of aorist 3rd plural forms. Probably an aorist of sambhavati: saṃ + √bhū + a, with the aorist stem sambh-, i.e. sambhuhesuṃ (sambhuṁsu) or sambhaviṃsu; the text's sambhutanti may be a badly transmitted or variant spelling. Could also be a present 3rd plural of a denominative/compound form, but the ending looks aorist. Analyzed here as aorist.

iccānusāsi.meaning_2: thus instructed; advised in this way
iccānusāsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of iti + anusāsi (aorist of anusāsati). The sandhi form is retained as written in the verse; may alternatively be taken as iti + anusāsi split at the head.
iccānusāsi.example_1: Iccānusāsi maṃ tāto, yathā maṃ anukampako.
iccānusāsi.translation_1: My compassionate father instructed me thus.

sopavāhano.meaning_2: golden and with its mount; together with its mounting
sopavāhano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse so + upavāhano; the same so refers back to pallaṅko. The related PEU entry instead takes saha + upavāhana, 'with attendants', commenting saparivāraṃ; the verse context (a golden couch) favours 'so upavāhano'.
sopavāhano.example_1: 140. ‘‘ Yo ca tassāsi pallaṅko, sovaṇṇo sopavāhano;
sopavāhano.translation_1: And the couch that was hers, which was golden and with its mount;

sahassapaṭiyatthato.meaning_2: of a thousand preparations; furnished in a thousand ways; with a thousand adornments
sahassapaṭiyatthato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural/ablative in -to in the text (sahassapaṭiyatthato); the corresponding entry sahassapaṭiyatthata is a doubtful reading. Alternative split sahassa + paṭiyatta (with a thousand preparations) from √yat; understood as number + adjective like sahassadibbakojavatthata.
sahassapaṭiyatthato.translation_1: with fifty canopies and a thousand celestial coverings;

kaṇṇaveṇṇāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a river in the Mahisaka country, said to issue from the Saṅkhapāla lake. Instrumental singular in the text: "at the bend of the Kaṇṇaveṇṇā river". The first element may be kaṇṇa (ear) but the name's formation is uncertain.
kaṇṇaveṇṇāya.example_1: So kañci ajānāpetvā uyyānā nikkhamitvā magadharaṭṭhaṃ atikkamitvā mahisakaraṭṭhe saṅkhapāladahato nāma nikkhantāya kaṇṇaveṇṇāya nadiyā nivattane candakapabbataṃ upanissāya paṇṇasālaṃ katvā tattha vasanto kasiṇaparikammaṃ katvā jhānābhiññā nibbattetvā uñchācariyāya yāpesi.
kaṇṇaveṇṇāya.translation_1: Without letting anyone know, he exited the royal park, surpassed the Magadha kingdom, and in the Mahisaka country, at the bend of the Kaṇṇaveṇṇā river which issues from a lake called Saṅkhapāla, relying on Candaka Mountain, he made a hut of leaves. Dwelling there, he performed the preparatory exercises for the kasina, developed jhānas and higher knowledges, and subsisted by gathering wild food.
kaṇṇaveṇṇāya.example_2: So tato paṭṭhāya nāgabhavanā nikkhamitvā kaṇṇaveṇṇāya nadiyā avidūre mahāmaggassa ca ekapadikamaggassa ca antare ekaṃ vammikaṃ parikkhipitvā uposathaṃ adhiṭṭhāya samādinnasīlo ‘‘ mama cammamaṃsādīhi atthikā cammamaṃsādīni harantū ’’ ti attānaṃ dānamukhe vissajjetvā vammikamatthake nipanno samaṇadhammaṃ karonto cātuddase pannarase vasitvā pāṭipade nāgabhavanaṃ gacchati.
kaṇṇaveṇṇāya.translation_2: From then on, having exited the Naga abode, not far from the Kaṇṇaveṇṇā river, between the main road and a narrow path, he coiled around an ant-hill. Having resolved to observe the Uposatha, and having undertaken the precepts, he offered himself as a gift, saying, ‘Let those who desire my skin, flesh, and so on, take them.’ Lying down on top of the ant-hill, practicing the ascetic life, he stayed on the fourteenth and fifteenth days [of the lunar fortnight] and went to the Naga realm on the day after the Uposatha.

kaṇṇaveṇṇanadito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in the text (nikkhamitvā ... nadito). Name of a river; nadī is feminine but the compound is treated here as a whole.
kaṇṇaveṇṇanadito.example_1: Tamenaṃ saṅkhapālo nāma nāgarājā mahantena parivārena kaṇṇaveṇṇanadito nikkhamitvā antarantarā upasaṅkamati.
kaṇṇaveṇṇanadito.translation_1: A king of snake-gods named Saṅkhapāla, having exited the Kaṇṇaveṇṇā river with a large retinue, would go to see him from time to time.

anuvicārāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be investigated; having had enquiries made
anuvicārāpetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of anuvicārāpeti (causative of anuvicarati). The prefix anu- is not separated from the root in √car, so family_root is 'anu vi √car'. In the sentence it refers to having a search or enquiry made for the missing father.
anuvicārāpetvā.example_1: Athassa putto pitaraṃ daṭṭhukāmo gataṭṭhānaṃ ajānanto anuvicārāpetvā ‘‘ asukaṭṭhāne nāma vasatī ’’ ti ñatvā tassa dassanatthāya mahantena parivārena tattha gantvā ekamante khandhavāraṃ nivāsetvā katipayehi amaccehi saddhiṃ assamapadābhimukho pāyāsi.
anuvicārāpetvā.translation_1: Then his son, desiring to see his father and not knowing where he had gone, had an investigation made. Having learned, 'He dwells in such-and-such a place,' he went there with a large retinue for the purpose of seeing him. Having set up camp in a discreet place, he set out towards the hermitage with a few ministers.

vikopayitvā.meaning_2: having cut up; having cut off; having destroyed
vikopayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of vikopeti (causative of √kup); glossed in the text as chinditvā. PEU splits as vi + kupa + ṇaya + tvā.
vikopayitvā.example_1: 149. ‘‘ Ito mayaṃ gantvā sakaṃ niketaṃ, ādāya satthāni vikopayitvā;
vikopayitvā.translation_1: 149. “From here, having gone to our own home, taking knives and cutting up [the flesh];

palokayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of paloketi (causative of palokati). The ending -yi is unusual; metrical or archaic variant of palokesi. The sandhi with maṃ is unmarked.
palokayī.example_1: 153. ‘‘ Gantvāna pācīnamukho muhuttaṃ, puṇṇehi nettehi palokayī maṃ;
palokayī.translation_1: 153. “Having gone facing the east for a moment, he looked at me with eyes full of tears;

vikopayitvāti.meaning_2: having destroyed; having ruined; having disturbed; having cut out
vikopayitvāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form is vikopayitvāti = vikopayitvā + iti; the -ti is a quotation ending, so the entry is for the absolutive. Causal absolutive in -tvā of vikopeti (caus of vikopati), literally 'having caused to be disturbed', hence 'having destroyed; having ruined'.

palokayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular; takes accusative object (maṃ). The present is palokati, not a common form; probably a variant of paloketi.
palokayi.example_1: Puṇṇehīti sopi muhuttaṃ pācīnābhimukho gantvā assupuṇṇehi nettehi maṃ palokayi.
palokayi.translation_1: With full [eyes] (puṇṇehī) [means that] he too, having gone facing the east for a moment, looked at me with eyes full of tears.

kaṇṇaveṇṇadahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, glossing rahadaṃ. Name of a lake associated with the Kaṇṇaveṇṇa river in the Jātaka stories.

kaṇṇaveṇṇatīraṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Place name. Accusative singular in the text, with anatikkanteyeva agreeing with it in the locative absolute.
kaṇṇaveṇṇatīraṃ.example_1: Dibbena meti nāgabhavane pamādaṃ anāpajjitvā mayi kaṇṇaveṇṇatīraṃ anatikkanteyeva dibbena parivārena mama purato pāturahosi.
kaṇṇaveṇṇatīraṃ.translation_1: For me with a divine [retinue] (dibbena me) [means that] he appeared before me with a divine retinue in the nāga realm, without falling into negligence, while I had not yet passed beyond the bank of the Kaṇṇaveṇṇa.

anāvakulā.meaning_2: not rugged; not uneven; with even shores
anāvakulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes the shores of a lake. Nominative plural in the verse, agreeing with a feminine noun. The commentary glosses it as na avakulā: free from high and low unevenness (ukkula-vikula), even.
anāvakulā.translation_1: 159. “Its shores are not rugged, it is beryl-hued, and there is an extremely delightful mango grove in all directions;
anāvakulā.example_2: Anāvakulāti na avakulā akhāṇumā upari ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā vā samasaṇṭhitā.
anāvakulā.translation_2: Its shores are not rugged (anāvakulā) means not low-lying, without stumps, or rather, free from an uneven, high and low state, but evenly arranged.

veḷuriyūpanīlā.meaning_2: dark blue like beryl; beryl-hued; dark blue because of beryl
veḷuriyūpanīlā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a pond in a nāga realm; in the text it is nominative singular feminine agreeing with pokkharaṇī. The commentary glosses it as veḷuriyena upanīlā.
veḷuriyūpanīlā.translation_1: 159. “Its shores are not rugged, it is beryl-hued, and there is an extremely delightful mango grove in all directions;
veḷuriyūpanīlā.example_2: Veḷuriyūpanīlāti veḷuriyena upanīlā, tasmiṃ nāgabhavane veḷuriyamayā pasannasalilā nīlobhāsā anekavaṇṇakamaluppalasañchannā pokkharaṇīti attho.
veḷuriyūpanīlā.translation_2: Beryl-hued (veḷuriyūpanīlā) means dark blue due to beryl; it means that in that nāga realm there is a pond made of beryl, with clear water, green-hued, and covered with lotuses and water lilies of various colors.

anāvakulāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The -ti is a quotation marker (iti) joined to the word; the entry is for the main word anāvakula. Negative compound of āvakula (turbid, muddy).

akhāṇumā.meaning_2: without stumps; free from tree stumps
akhāṇumā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text akhāṇumā is an instrumental singular used adverbially, describing the river shore as free of stumps; the whole phrase is glossed by samasaṇṭhitā.
akhāṇumā.example_1: Anāvakulāti na avakulā akhāṇumā upari ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā vā samasaṇṭhitā.
akhāṇumā.translation_1: Its shores are not rugged (anāvakulā) means not low-lying, without stumps, or rather, free from an uneven, high and low state, but evenly arranged.

ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā.meaning_2: free from being uneven and level; without irregularities; even
ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a place free from highs and lows, i.e. level. Feminine ū-stem adjective here agreeing with the noun it modifies.
ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā.example_1: Anāvakulāti na avakulā akhāṇumā upari ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā vā samasaṇṭhitā.
ukkulavikulabhāvarahitā.translation_1: Its shores are not rugged (anāvakulā) means not low-lying, without stumps, or rather, free from an uneven, high and low state, but evenly arranged.

veḷuriyūpanīlāti.meaning_2: blue as lapis lazuli; of the deep blue of beryl
veḷuriyūpanīlāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi with -ti; the main word is veḷuriyūpanīlā (nominative singular fem of a bahubbīhi). veḷuriya = beryl or lapis lazuli, upanīla = deep blue or greenish blue. It describes a dark blue like beryl.

upanīlā.meaning_2: dark blue; dark green; bluish; greenish
