nayituṃ.translation_1: Having killed many of the Madda family, to bring you, Pabhāvatī.”
nayituṃ.example_2: Bahuṃ maddakulaṃ hantvā nayituṃ tanti bahumaddarājakulaṃ hanitvā balakkārena taṃ netuṃ samatthoti.
nayituṃ.translation_2: Bahuṃ maddakulaṃ hantvā nayituṃ taṃ means, “capable of having killed many of the Madda royal family and bringing her by force.”

tyasmīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolving to ti + asmi + iti (ti + asmi + iti → tyasmīti); an utterance quoted as "I am that", nominative singular asmi with the quotative iti. Occurs in the Jātaka prose commentary.

vikuddhabhāvañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (ca = 'and').
vikuddhabhāvañca.example_1: Sabbaṃ teti vikuddhabhāvañca idāni appiyakaraṇañca ubhayaṃ te idaṃ sabbameva paṭijānāmi.
vikuddhabhāvañca.translation_1: Sabbaṃ te means, “I acknowledge to you both the state of being angry and the doing of unpleasant things now; I confess all this to you.”

titikkhisanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Desiderative/intensive form of √tij 3. Here 3rd plural future of titikkhati; also analysed as title of √tij 3.}

katamassukammo.meaning_2: whose beard-trimming has been done; with his beard trimmed
katamassukammo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kataṃ + massu? Or kata + massu? Locative singular in the text: "katamassukammo" = kata + massu + kamma? Relative adjective modifying "so".
katamassukammo.example_1: So katamassukammo sīsaṃnhāto sabbālaṅkārapaṭimaṇḍito amaccādīhi parivuto ‘‘ pāsādaṃ abhiruhissāmī ’’ ti disā viloketvā apphoṭesi.
katamassukammo.translation_1: With his beard trimmed, his head bathed, and adorned with all ornaments, he was surrounded by ministers and others. Thinking, “I will ascend to the palace,” he contemplated the directions and clapped his hands.

vipalāyiṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural in -iṃsu of vipalāyati, with the prefix vi- added to palāyati. The text describes the nobles fleeing in fear.
vipalāyiṃsu.translation_1: the nobles fled, afflicted by the fear of Kusa’s roar.

vipalāyiṃsūti.meaning_2: fled away in various directions; ran about, it is said
vipalāyiṃsūti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vipalāyiṃsu (aorist 3rd plural of vipalāyati) with iti; the -ti marks a quotation. Alternative analysis: vipalāyiṃ + iti is less likely.

khamāpakā.meaning_2: one who asks for pardon; one who requests forgiveness
khamāpakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative agent noun; nominative plural khamāpakā in the text, glossed by the commentary as yācakā (those who ask).
khamāpakā.translation_1: Yācakā means those who will ask for pardon (khamāpakā) from Soṇa the Wise for my sake (mamatthāya).

ābandhitabbāni.meaning_2: to be fastened (to); to be tied on (to)
ābandhitabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The word in the text is neuter nominative plural, agreeing with bhaṇḍāni: 'the things to be fastened to elephants, horses and chariots'. glossed by the commentary's ābandhanāni.
ābandhitabbāni.translation_1: Ābandhanāni means “take up the equipment (bhaṇḍāni) that should be fastened (ābandhitabbāni) to the elephants, horses, and chariots.”

patibodhayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative aorist, 3rd singular, of patibodhayati (pati + √budh, caus). The text has the common aorist ending -i for causative verbs. The PEU analysis budha + ṇaya is a variant of the same causative formation.
patibodhayi.translation_1: having entered the hut of leaves, he informed his father.”

parikīrentīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the verb carries the quotative -ti (parikīrentīti = parikīrenti + iti); alternative analysis: parikirenti (3rd plural of parikirati), but the formation here is causative parikīreti.

parikīrayanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The explanation given in the text is a gloss, not a second reading: 'they scatter all around'. A possible alternative analysis is a denominative from parikīra.
parikīrayanti.translation_1: “Surrounding” (parikīrentī) means ‘they encompass him all around, in all directions’.

massame.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text ('in this ashram'). The related PEU entry massu (beard) is a different word. Possibly a variant of assama (hermitage).
massame.example_1: 140. ‘‘ Ye ca santi samītāro, yakkhāni idha massame;
massame.translation_1: “And those yakkhas who are gathered here in this ashram,

upanissaja.meaning_2: releases; gives up; hands over; offers
upanissaja.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 2nd singular in -hi, used in the Jātaka verse; the PEU gives ‘give up, offer’. The form could also be analysed as an aorist, but the imperative fits the sentence.
upanissaja.translation_1: “Indeed, this has been advocated by civil people; release this to me;

upanissajāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form upanissajāti is upanissajati with the final -ti lengthened (metrical or scribal). Third person singular; the PEU gloss is 'gives up or offers'.

abhivāreti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of abhivārati (to ward off, restrain); here in the sense of preventing someone from merit. Third person singular present in the text.
abhivāreti.example_1: Taṃ manti taṃ maṃ evaṃ sammāpaṭipannampi bhātā soṇapaṇḍito tamhā puññā abhivāreti.
abhivāreti.translation_1: “That me” (taṃ maṃ) means, “That me, even though practicing correctly, my brother Soṇa the Wise prevents from that merit.”

parihāpayaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle in -ṃ (nominative singular masculine), used as a noun meaning 'the one who neglects'. Absolutive-like form in -aṃ; the caus. conveys causing to increase? No: parihāpayati suggests 'causes to fall away'.
parihāpayaṃ.translation_1: O Great King, whoever neglects the ancient family custom,

parihāpayanti.meaning_2: cause to decrease; diminish; make decline; deprive (of)
parihāpayanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of parihāyati; 3rd plural present in the text (-nti for -ti). Some editions read parihāpenti, which is more regular.

upasiṅghāyituṃ.meaning_2: to smell; to sniff at; to kiss (by sniffing)
upasiṅghāyituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive from upasiṅghāyati (upa + siṃ + ghāya, with ghāya from √ghā). In the text it refers to sniffing/kissing the head (sīse upasiṅghāyituṃ) out of affection.
upasiṅghāyituṃ.example_1: Athassa mātā āsanā vuṭṭhāya,‘‘ tāta soṇapaṇḍita, cirappavuttho te kaniṭṭho, evaṃ cirāgatampi taṃ yācituṃ na visahāmi, mayañhi taṃ nissitā, idāni pana tayā anuññātā ahaṃ etaṃ brahmacārinaṃ bāhāhi upagūhitvā sīse upasiṅghāyituṃ labheyyan ’’ ti imamatthaṃ pakāsentī gāthamāha –
upasiṅghāyituṃ.translation_1: Then his mother, having risen from her seat, revealing this matter, uttered the verse: “Dear Soṇa the Wise, your younger brother has been long absent. Even though he has come after so long, I do not dare to plead with him, for we indeed rely on you. But now, having been allowed by you, I may embrace this follower of the spiritual life with my arms and kiss his head.”

labhatū.meaning_2: let him receive; may he obtain; may he get
labhatū.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Imperative 3rd singular in -tu, used as a blessing or wish. Written labhatū before the quotative ti (sandhi of -tu + ti).
labhatū.translation_1: “Let him receive a thousand (coins) every day.”
labhatū.example_2: ‘‘ devi, kiṃ kathesi, tava dhītā sakalajambudīpe aggarājānaṃ ‘ virūpo ’ ti chaḍḍetvā gatamagge padavalañje avinaṭṭheyeva maccuṃ nalāṭenādāya āgatā, idāni attano rūpaṃ nissāya īdisaṃ phalaṃ labhatū ’’ ti.
labhatū.translation_2: “O queen, what are you saying? Your daughter, having rejected the excellent king of all Jambudīpa as ‘ugly,’ has returned, taking death by the forehead even before her footprints on the traveled path have vanished. Now, relying on her own beauty, let her receive such a result!”

varate.grammar: pr, caus of varati?; or pr of varati
varate.meaning_2: desires; wishes for; chooses; asks (for); woos
varate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Middle/reflexive 3rd singular varate (= varati), 'desires; wishes for'; the PEU glosses it 'he wants'. The syntax maggo ... mātā taṃ varate ise is obscure; possibly 'the mother ... desires you, O sage'. Could also be an optative-style form, but taken as present indicative.
varate.example_1: Maggo saggassa lokassa, mātā taṃ varate ise.
varate.translation_1: The mother is the path to the heavenly world, O sage; she desires you.
varate.example_2: Maggo saggassa lokassa, mātā taṃ varate ise ’’ ti.
varate.translation_2: The mother is the path to the heavenly world, O sage; she desires you.’

gottī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Glossed in the text as gopāyikā; a feminine agent noun from the root √gup. Nominative singular in the verse.
gottī.translation_1: 164. ‘Previously giving milk-savour and a protector, a mother endowed with merit;

varati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present, used in the commentary to gloss icchati with varati.
varati.example_1: Mātā tanti mama mātā maṃ na icchati, taṃ varati icchati.
varati.translation_1: Mātā taṃ: ‘My mother does not desire me; she desires you, she wants you.’

gottīti.meaning_2: woman of (good) lineage; gentlewoman; one who is caring
gottīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Formed from gotta (lineage, family) with the feminine suffix -ī; the PEU analysis Gupa+ta+ī points to √gup with the -ta participle (gutta, 'guarded, protected'), giving the secondary sense 'caring woman'. The -ti in the text is the quotative particle.

māhārājakulāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural: māhārājakulāni. Compound with mahā at the front, showing the lengthened vowel.
māhārājakulāni.example_1: Tadā mātāpitaro māhārājakulāni ahesuṃ, nandapaṇḍito ānando, manojarājā sāriputto, ekasatarājāno asītimahātherā ceva aññataratherā ca, catuvīsati akkhobhaṇiyo buddhaparisā, soṇapaṇḍito pana ahameva ahosinti.
māhārājakulāni.translation_1: “Then the mothers and fathers were the royal families; Nanda the Wise was Ānanda; King Manoja was Sāriputta; the one hundred and one kings were the eighty great elders and certain other elders; the twenty-four akkhobhaṇī were the Buddha’s assembly; but Soṇa the Wise was I indeed.”

abhivāsitasattatimamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of abhivāsita (perfumed; scented) and sattatima (seventieth). Locative singular in the text; maybe an epithet or name of a place.
abhivāsitasattatimamhi.example_1: Atha soṇasunandavaro ca puna, abhivāsitasattatimamhi suteti.
abhivāsitasattatimamhi.translation_1: And again, the noble Soṇasunanda is heard in the splendidly perfumed seventieth.

apphoṭiṃsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd plural aorist in the text, paired with unnadiṃsu. The simplex is apphoṭeti (Caus of ā + √phuṭ), from which this aorist is formed; the doubled p is sandhi after the prefix.
apphoṭiṃsu.example_1: Manussā taṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā unnadiṃsu apphoṭiṃsu, sañjātasomanassā nānābharaṇāni khipiṃsu, tāni hatthissa sarīraṃ paṭicchādayiṃsu.
apphoṭiṃsu.translation_1: The people, on seeing that miracle, raised a loud cry and snapped their fingers. With joy arisen in them, they threw many ornaments, and these covered the elephant’s body.

sāgalo.meaning_2: Sāgala; king of Sāgala; name of a king
sāgalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of the king of Sāgala city in the Mahiṃsaka kingdom; nominative singular in the text. PEU treats it as derived from the place name sāgala.
sāgalo.example_1: Atīte mahiṃsakaraṭṭhe sāgalanagare sāgalo nāma rājā dhammena rajjaṃ kāresi.
sāgalo.translation_1: In the past, in the kingdom of Mahiṃsaka, in the city of Sāgala, a king called Sāgalo ruled the kingdom by law and right.

nirūpakārena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text instrumental singular in a bahubbīhi phrase 'with me, who am useless'. Sometimes analysed as ni + upakāra with shortening of the vowel before the compound.
nirūpakārena.example_1: Pakkamantīti ete channavuti haṃsasahassā ñātivihaṅgamā maṃ chaḍḍetvā gacchanti, tvampi gaccha, mā idha vāsaṃ ākaṅkhi, evañhi pāsena baddhe mayi sahāyatā nāma natthi, na hi te ahaṃ idāni kiñci sahāyakiccaṃ kātuṃ sakkhissāmi, kiṃ te mayā nirūpakārena, papañcaṃ akatvā gacchevāti vadati.
nirūpakārena.translation_1: Pakkamanti means: ‘These ninety-six thousand kinsfolk geese have abandoned me and are going. You too, go; do not desire dwelling here. For indeed, when I am bound by a snare, there is no such thing as companionship. Indeed, I will not be able to render any friendly service for you now. What benefit is there for you with me, who am useless? Go without making delay,’ thus he says.

upāsitvā.meaning_2: having attended upon; having served; having associated with
upāsitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā; the form in the text agrees with the Peu split upa+āsa+tvā.
upāsitvā.example_1: Sukhitaṃ taṃ upāsitvā, dukkhitaṃ taṃ kathaṃ jahe.
upāsitvā.translation_1: Having attended upon you when you were happy, how could I abandon you when you are suffering?
upāsitvā.example_2: Tattha gacche vāti, mahārāja, ahaṃ ito gaccheyyaṃ vā na vā, nāhaṃ tena gamanena vā agamanena vā amaro siyaṃ, ahañhi ito gatopi agatopi maraṇato amuttova, ito pubbe pana sukhitaṃ taṃ upāsitvā idāni dukkhitaṃ taṃ kathaṃ jaheyyanti vadati.
upāsitvā.translation_2: Therein, gacche vā means: ‘Great King, whether I go from here or not, I would not become immortal by that going or not going. Indeed, whether I go from here or not, I am not freed from death. But having attended upon you when you were happy before this, how could I abandon you now that you are suffering?’ thus he says.

sañcajaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle sañcajanta (accusative singular sañcajaṃ in the text) meaning 'sacrificing; giving up (one's life)'. The reading and meaning are uncertain.
sañcajaṃ.translation_1: Sacrificing your life in such a [futile] way, what benefit would you illuminate?”

tvevaṃ.meaning_2: but thus; however in this way
tvevaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tu + evaṃ (tu assimilated to t). The commentary glosses api tvevaṃ as api tu evaṃ. Part of the phrase api tvevaṃ gate kāle.
tvevaṃ.example_1: 12. ‘‘ Api tvevaṃ gate kāle, yaṃ khaṇḍaṃ ñātinaṃ mayā;
tvevaṃ.translation_1: 12. “But indeed, at such a time, the portion of relatives entrusted by me,
tvevaṃ.example_2: Api tvevaṃ gate kāleti api tu evaṃ gate kāle mayi imasmiṃ ṭhāne pāsena baddhe.
tvevaṃ.translation_2: Api tvevaṃ gate kāle means: ‘But indeed, at such a time, when I am bound by a snare in this place.’

vegenabhikkamma.meaning_2: having approached quickly; having gone up to swiftly
vegenabhikkamma.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vegeno and abhikkamma in the text. abhikkamma is an absolutive participle from abhikkamati (to advance; to approach), so together this means 'having approached swiftly'. This is a compound verb (vegena + abhikkamma).
vegenabhikkamma.example_1: 16. ‘‘ So ca vegenabhikkamma, āsajja parame dije;
vegenabhikkamma.translation_1: 16. “And he, having swiftly approached, came upon the excellent birds;

vimatoyeva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Written vimatoyeva for vimatī + eva (sandhi, dropped final -ī before e). Ī-stem adjective used nominative singular here. Can also be analysed as vi + mata + ī.
vimatoyeva.translation_1: 18. “Then he, indeed filled with uncertainty, spoke to the golden-colored ones,

pāṇasañcajanaṃ.meaning_2: sacrificing one's life; giving up life
pāṇasañcajanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of pāṇa and sañcajana (from saṃ + √caj). Appears twice in the same sentence, nominative/accusative singular neuter.
pāṇasañcajanaṃ.example_1: Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – tayi pāṇaṃ cajantepi acajantepi mama jīvitassa abhāvā yaṃ tava pāṇasañcajanaṃ, taṃ andhena tamasi kataṃ viya kiñcideva rūpakammaṃ apaccakkhaguṇaṃ, tādise tava apaccakkhaguṇe pāṇasañcajane tvaṃ pāṇaṃ sañcajanto kamatthaṃ joteyyāsīti.
pāṇasañcajanaṃ.translation_1: This is what is said: ‘Whether you sacrifice your life or not, due to the absence of my life, that sacrificing of your life is like some visible action without clear benefit, done by a blind person in darkness. In such a sacrifice of your life, which is without clear benefit, what benefit would you illuminate by sacrificing your life?’

pāṇasañcajane.meaning_2: sacrificing of life; giving up of life
pāṇasañcajane.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, agreeing with the repeated pāṇasañcajane. Built from pāṇa and the noun sañcajana from √caj with saṃ; the whole compound is left without a root.
pāṇasañcajane.example_1: Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – tayi pāṇaṃ cajantepi acajantepi mama jīvitassa abhāvā yaṃ tava pāṇasañcajanaṃ, taṃ andhena tamasi kataṃ viya kiñcideva rūpakammaṃ apaccakkhaguṇaṃ, tādise tava apaccakkhaguṇe pāṇasañcajane tvaṃ pāṇaṃ sañcajanto kamatthaṃ joteyyāsīti.
pāṇasañcajane.translation_1: This is what is said: ‘Whether you sacrifice your life or not, due to the absence of my life, that sacrificing of your life is like some visible action without clear benefit, done by a blind person in darkness. In such a sacrifice of your life, which is without clear benefit, what benefit would you illuminate by sacrificing your life?’

sañcajanto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle of sañcajati (saṃ + √caj). Masculine nominative singular in the text.
sañcajanto.example_1: Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – tayi pāṇaṃ cajantepi acajantepi mama jīvitassa abhāvā yaṃ tava pāṇasañcajanaṃ, taṃ andhena tamasi kataṃ viya kiñcideva rūpakammaṃ apaccakkhaguṇaṃ, tādise tava apaccakkhaguṇe pāṇasañcajane tvaṃ pāṇaṃ sañcajanto kamatthaṃ joteyyāsīti.
sañcajanto.translation_1: This is what is said: ‘Whether you sacrifice your life or not, due to the absence of my life, that sacrificing of your life is like some visible action without clear benefit, done by a blind person in darkness. In such a sacrifice of your life, which is without clear benefit, what benefit would you illuminate by sacrificing your life?’

abhisañcikkhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form of abhisañcikkhati; the doubling -ñc- is sandhi for abhi + saṃ + cikkhati. The PEU entry abhisañcikkha is probably an absolutive (a variant of abhisañcikkhitvā) rather than a present. No sentence is available to confirm.

sañcalesumāsanāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text form is sandhi sañcalesuṃ + āsanā ('shook the seats'). 3rd plural aorist of sañcalati (saṃ + √cal).

vimatoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text vimatoti = vimata + ti, the quotative particle; the entry is for vimata. PEU derives it from vimati with suffix ṇa; sometimes analysed as vi + mata (pp of √man).

saṃruḷho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of saṃruhati. Nominative singular masculine in the text, describing pādo.
saṃruḷho.example_1: Tassa mettacittānubhāvena bodhisattassa pāde sirā sirāhi, maṃsaṃ maṃsena, cammaṃ cammena ghaṭitaṃ, tāvadeva pādo saṃruḷho sañjātachavisañjātalomo ahosi abaddhapādena nibbiseso.
saṃruḷho.translation_1: By the power of his mind of loving-kindness, the veins united with veins, flesh with flesh, and skin with skin on the Bodhisatta’s foot. At that very moment, the foot healed, and new skin and hair grew, indistinguishable from the unbound foot.

upapādayi.meaning_2: accomplished; carried out; fulfilled; put into effect
upapādayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative upapādayati. In the verse kammunā upapādayi means 'he carried it out by his action'. PEU suggests upa + pada + ṇe + ī.
upapādayi.example_1: 40. ‘‘ Tassa taṃ vacanaṃ sutvā, kammunā upapādayi;
upapādayi.translation_1: 40. “Upon hearing his word, he acted accordingly;

upapādayīti.meaning_2: causes to finish; causes to fulfil; causes to be sufficient
upapādayīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text form upapādayīti is upapādayī + iti, aorist 3rd singular of the causative with the quotation -iti; PEU's -ṇe- analysis differs.

kicci.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kicci sits between pariccajantā and attano; koci + ci with sandhi, or a written form of 'koci'. The sentence is difficult and the reading is uncertain.
kicci.example_1: Nāvakaṅkhantīti uraṃ datvā pariccajantā kicci attano jīvitaṃ na patthenti, jīvitañca cajitvā tavevatthaṃ karonti.
kicci.translation_1: They do not desire (nāvakaṅkhanti) means, "Giving their chests, sacrificing their lives, do they not desire their own lives? And do they abandon their lives and act for your welfare alone?"

samapothayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Metrically shortened form of sampothesi (aorist 3rd singular of sampotheti). The PEU analysis (saṃ + putha + ṇaya + ī) is uncertain; causative sign *e is more likely. Object is 'you' (daṇḍena = with a stick).
samapothayi.translation_1: 65. “Did the fowler rush up and strike you with a stick?

rasmāsu.meaning_2: ray of light; radiance; beam; brightness
rasmāsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text (rasmāsu). The reading could also be rasmiṃsu; the sense here is metaphorical, 'radiance' or 'majesty' rather than a physical beam. The PEU entry conflates rasmi (ray) with rasmi (rope).
rasmāsu.example_1: Na cāyaṃ kiñci rasmāsu, sattūva samapajjatha.
rasmāsu.translation_1: Nor did he act towards us in any way like an enemy.

pāmucī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text. The form is unusual; perhaps metrical or corrupt for pamuñci. Translated 'released' in the sentence.
pāmucī.example_1: Tato maṃ pāmucī pāsā, anuññāsi sukhena ca.
pāmucī.translation_1: Then he released me from the snare and allowed us to go comfortably.

svāgatañcevidaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of svāgataṃ (welcome), ca eva (and indeed), and idaṃ (this). Here svāgataṃ is neuter nominative singular; the compound is a whole clause meaning 'and this is welcome'.
svāgatañcevidaṃ.translation_1: 70. “You are welcome, sirs, and I am pleased by the sight;

rasmāsūti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of rasmi + āsu + iti; rasmi is feminine i-stem, locative plural rasmīsu, with āsu in the text. The word is unclear without context; possibly a quotation.

upabhottuṃ.meaning_2: to enjoy; to use; to make use of
upabhottuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of upabhuñjati, used here with dāna ('for giving, for enjoying'). The PEU gives upa+bhuja+tuṃ; the doubling of t is the usual infinitive suffix -tuṃ.
upabhottuṃ.example_1: 73. ‘‘ Dānatthaṃ upabhottuṃ vā, yaṃ caññaṃ upakappati;
upabhottuṃ.translation_1: 73. “For giving, for enjoying, or whatever is appropriate;
upabhottuṃ.example_2: Yaṃ caññaṃ upakappatīti puññakāmatāya dānatthaṃ vā chattaṃ ussāpetvā rajjameva upabhottuṃ vā yaṃ vā aññaṃ tumhākaṃ ruccati, taṃ karotha, etaṃ dadāmi vo vittaṃ, saddhiṃyeva setacchattena mama santakaṃ issariyaṃ vissajjāmi voti.
upabhottuṃ.translation_2: Or whatever is appropriate (yaṃ caññaṃ upakappati) means: whether for the purpose of giving, desiring merit, or for enjoying the kingdom itself by raising the umbrella, or whatever else is pleasing to you, do that. ‘This wealth I give to you, and I relinquish to you my lordship, which belongs to me, together with the white canopy’ — this is the meaning.
